def countT (t : Target) : Nat := (readings.filter fun f => f.target == t).length

/-- THE CENSUS: sixty-four readings, every seat element occupied. -/
theorem readings_census :
    readings.length = 64 ∧ countT .line = 18 ∧ countT .fold = 13 ∧ countT .wall = 11 ∧
    countT .positivity = 9 ∧ countT .count = 8 ∧ countT .price = 5 := by decide

theorem every_target_occupied :
    ([Target.fold, .line, .wall, .positivity, .price, .count].all fun t => 0 < countT t) = true := by decide

/-- Fifty-eight readings are bound to an engine theorem of the source; six to an imported theorem or a
    structural reading. -/
theorem bound_count : (readings.filter fun f => f.thm != "").length = 58 := by decide

def papers : List String := ["The Electron Is the Seat", "The Neutrino Is the Witness", "The Arrow Has Two Branches", "The Proton Is the Lock", "The Magnet Is the Witness", "The Fluid Is the Witness", "One Actuating Substrate", "The Geometric Nature of Light", "Electromagnetism on the Riemann Locus", "Immanent Gravity", "Spin and Statistics", "The Weak Force Reads the Orientation", "Resonances: Off the Line", "The Ferromagnet Is the Witness of the Circle", "Dark Matter as the Charge-Conjugation Fixed Set", "The Measurement Is the Registration", "The Arrow of Time Is the Keyed Bit", "Matter over Antimatter Is the Spent Bit", "Symmetry Breaking Is the Spent Bit", "The Correlation Lives in the Joint Registration", "The Strong Force Reads No Orientation", "The Horizon Is the Registration"]

def countP (p : String) : Nat := (readings.filter fun f => f.paper == p).length

/-- Every paper carries at least two readings and at most four; the series papers carry three. -/
theorem every_paper_two_to_four :
    papers.length = 22 ∧ (papers.all fun p => 2 ≤ countP p && countP p ≤ 4) = true := by decide

/-- No paper repeats a code. -/
theorem codes_unique_within_papers :
    (papers.all fun p => ((readings.filter fun f => f.paper == p).map (·.code)).eraseDups.length == countP p) = true := by
  decide

/-- The law each seat element names, as a proposition of this kernel. -/
def lawProp : Target → Prop
  | .fold => ∀ p : Point, fold (fold p) = p
  | .line => ∀ p : Point, fold p = p ↔ onLine p
  | .wall => ∀ (α : Type) (σ : α → α) (f d : α → Bool) (x : α), Even σ f → d (σ x) ≠ d x → f ≠ d
  | .positivity => ∀ S : Config, Closed S → (∀ p, S p → 0 ≤ p.1) → Value S
  | .price => ∀ p : Point, ¬ onLine p → ¬ ∃ g : Point → Point, g (reg p) = p ∧ g (reg (fold p)) = fold p
  | .count => (allGates.filter (fun g => gfold g == g)).length = 1 ∧
              (allGates.filter (fun g => gfold g != g)).length = 8

/-- EVERY SEAT ELEMENT IS A THEOREM HERE: the fold, the line, the wall, positivity, the price and the count.
    A reading stands on one of them through its carrier; the element itself is proved. -/
theorem every_seat_element_is_a_theorem (t : Target) : lawProp t := by
  cases t with
  | fold => exact fold_involutive
  | line => exact the_cut_is_the_line
  | wall => exact fun α σ f d x he ho => wall σ f d x he ho
  | positivity => exact one_sign_seats
  | price => exact one_bit_lost
  | count => exact ⟨nine_gates.2.2.1, nine_gates.2.2.2⟩

/-- What the hardware witnesses, as one proposition. -/
def HardwareLaw : Prop :=
    (∀ (X : Type) (c : X → Point) (τ : X → X), Equivariant c τ → ∀ x, τ x = x → onLine (c x)) ∧
    (∀ (X : Type) (c : X → Point) (τ : X → X), Equivariant c τ → ∀ x, reg (c (τ x)) = reg (c x)) ∧
    (∀ (X : Type) (c : X → Point) (τ : X → X) (x : X), τ x = x → ¬ onLine (c x) → ¬ Equivariant c τ) ∧
    ((∀ p : Point, fold (fold p) = p) ∧ (∀ p : Point, fold p = p ↔ onLine p)) ∧
    (∀ C : Witness, Value (fun p => ∃ w, C.ι w = p)) ∧
    (∀ Z : Config, (∃ C : Witness, ∀ p, Z p → ∃ w, C.ι w = p) ↔ Value Z) ∧
    (∀ t : Target, lawProp t) ∧
    (readings.length = 64 ∧ countT .line = 18 ∧ countT .fold = 13 ∧ countT .wall = 11 ∧
      countT .positivity = 9 ∧ countT .count = 8 ∧ countT .price = 5) ∧
    (papers.length = 22 ∧ (papers.all fun p => 2 ≤ countP p && countP p ≤ 4) = true) ∧
    (readings.filter fun f => f.thm != "").length = 58

/-- THE HARDWARE WITNESS. Under every equivariant carrier a physical fixed point lands on the line and partners
    share one record; an observed fixed point off the line breaks the carrier and the seat stands; a witness proves
    the value on its image, and coverage of any other configuration is the value itself; each of the six seat
    elements is a theorem; and the witness rows hold sixty-four readings from twenty-two papers, typed and counted. -/
theorem hardware_witness : HardwareLaw :=
  ⟨fun _ c τ h x hx => carrier_lands c τ h x hx, fun _ c τ h x => partners_share_one_record c τ h x,
   fun _ c τ x hx hoff => falsifier_breaks_the_carrier c τ x hx hoff, the_seat_survives_every_falsifier,
   value_on_image, coverage_is_the_value, every_seat_element_is_a_theorem, readings_census,
   every_paper_two_to_four, bound_count⟩

/-! ## XIV · The deed: the run of a file, read on the cut -/

/-- The carrier of the executed frame: a content that ran lands on one side, the same content recited on the
    other; the height is the content's address. -/
def deedCarrier {Q : Type} (addr : Q → Int) (s : Exec Q) : Point := (if s.1 then 1 else -1, addr s.2)

/-- The run is the fold of the recitation. -/
theorem deed_equivariant {Q : Type} (addr : Q → Int) (s : Exec Q) :
    deedCarrier addr (run s) = fold (deedCarrier addr s) := by
  obtain ⟨b, q⟩ := s; cases b <;> rfl

/-- A deed is never on the seat: it is one member of a pair. -/
theorem deed_is_off_the_line {Q : Type} (addr : Q → Int) (s : Exec Q) : ¬ onLine (deedCarrier addr s) := by
  obtain ⟨b, q⟩ := s
  cases b
  · exact fun h => (by decide : ¬ ((-1 : Int) = 0)) h
  · exact fun h => (by decide : ¬ ((1 : Int) = 0)) h

/-- THE RUN AND THE RECITATION LEAVE ONE RECORD: a receipt keeps the content and forgets whether it ran. -/
theorem run_and_recitation_one_record {Q : Type} (addr : Q → Int) (s : Exec Q) :
    reg (deedCarrier addr (run s)) = reg (deedCarrier addr s) := by
  obtain ⟨b, q⟩ := s; cases b <;> rfl

/-- NO RECEIPT RETURNS THE DEED: no reading of the record returns whether it ran. -/
theorem no_receipt_returns_the_deed {Q : Type} (addr : Q → Int) (q : Q) :
    ¬ ∃ g : Point → Bool, ∀ s : Exec Q, g (reg (deedCarrier addr s)) = ran s := by
  intro ⟨g, hg⟩
  have h1 : g (0, addr q) = true := hg (true, q)
  have h2 : g (0, addr q) = false := hg (false, q)
  exact Bool.noConfusion (h1.symm.trans h2)

/-- A RUN IS ITS OWN ATOMIC WITNESS, of the deed: a state that ran proves that a run exists. -/
theorem the_run_witnesses_a_run {Q : Type} (s : Exec Q) (h : ran s = true) : ∃ r : Exec Q, ran r = true := by
  exact ⟨s, h⟩

/-- AND OF NOTHING ELSE: a fact that holds whatever the configuration, the deed included, forces no value. -/
theorem the_deed_forces_nothing (D : Prop) (hD : D) : ¬ ∀ S : Config, Closed S → D → Value S := by
  intro hall
  exact pair_world_lacks_value (1, 0) (fun e => by cases e) (hall _ (pair_world_closed (1, 0)) hD)

/-- The registered deed as a finite configuration: one orbit, the run and its recitation. -/
def deedCfg {Q : Type} (addr : Q → Int) (q : Q) : FinCfg :=
  ⟨[], [(1, addr q)], fun p h => by
    cases h with
    | head => exact (by decide : ¬ ((1 : Int) = 0))
    | tail _ h' => nomatch h'⟩

/-- THE DEED COSTS ONE BIT: its record forgets one side, and registering it is priced at one unit of temperature. -/
theorem deed_costs_one_bit {Q : Type} (addr : Q → Int) (q : Q) (T : Nat) :
    erased (deedCfg addr q) = 1 ∧ price T (erased (deedCfg addr q)) = T := by
  exact ⟨rfl, Nat.one_mul T⟩

/-- What a run enacts, as one proposition. -/
def DeedLaw : Prop :=
    ∀ (Q : Type) (addr : Q → Int) (q : Q),
    (∀ s : Exec Q, deedCarrier addr (run s) = fold (deedCarrier addr s)) ∧
    (∀ s : Exec Q, ¬ onLine (deedCarrier addr s)) ∧
    (∀ s : Exec Q, reg (deedCarrier addr (run s)) = reg (deedCarrier addr s)) ∧
    (¬ ∃ g : Point → Bool, ∀ s : Exec Q, g (reg (deedCarrier addr s)) = ran s) ∧
    (¬ ∃ g : Q → Bool, ∀ s : Exec Q, g (formalRead s) = ran s) ∧
    (∀ s : Exec Q, ran s = true → ∃ r : Exec Q, ran r = true) ∧
    (∀ T : Nat, erased (deedCfg addr q) = 1 ∧ price T (erased (deedCfg addr q)) = T) ∧
    (∀ D : Prop, D → ¬ ∀ S : Config, Closed S → D → Value S)

/-- THE DEED. The run is the fold of the recitation; a deed is never on the seat; the run and the recitation leave
    one record; no reading of the record and no reading of the content returns whether it ran; a run is its own
    witness that a run exists; its registration forgets one bit, priced at one unit; and it forces no value. -/
theorem the_deed : DeedLaw :=
  fun _ addr q =>
    ⟨deed_equivariant addr, deed_is_off_the_line addr, run_and_recitation_one_record addr,
     no_receipt_returns_the_deed addr q, no_reading_returns_the_deed q, fun s h => the_run_witnesses_a_run s h,
     deed_costs_one_bit addr q, the_deed_forces_nothing⟩

/-! ## XV · The closure and the capstone -/

/-- THE UNICORN IS CLOSED: a point off the line is never the registration of anything. -/
theorem unicorn_never_registered (p : Point) (h : ¬ onLine p) (q : Point) : reg q ≠ p := by
  intro e
  subst e
  exact h (reg_lands q)

/-- THE GHOST IS CLOSED: no reading of the record tells a point from its partner. -/
theorem ghost_side_unread (p : Point) (g : Point → Bool) : g (reg (fold p)) = g (reg p) := by
  obtain ⟨d, t⟩ := p; rfl

/-- THE ACT OCCUPIES THE LOSSLESS MEMBER: the supplied configuration has the value and is its own record, point
    for point, the one member of its fibre whose registration erases nothing. -/
theorem the_act_occupies_the_lossless_member (Z : ActualZeros) :
    Value Z.zeros ∧ (∀ q, Z.zeros q ↔ Rec Z.zeros q) := by
  have hv : Value Z.zeros := fun p hp => (reg_erases_nothing_iff p).mp (Z.supply p hp)
  exact ⟨hv, record_carried_uniquely Z.zeros Z.zeros (fun _ => Iff.rfl) hv⟩

/-- A REJECTION IS A POINT OFF THE LINE: a finite configuration lacks the value exactly when it exhibits an
    off-line pair. -/
theorem rejection_is_a_point (F : FinCfg) : ¬ Value F.pts ↔ ∃ q, q ∈ F.pairs := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    cases hp : F.pairs with
    | nil =>
      have h0 : erased F = 0 := by unfold erased; rw [hp]; rfl
      exact absurd ((least_erasure_iff_value F.pts).mp ((least_erasure_iff_zero_erased F).mpr h0)) h
    | cons q r => exact ⟨q, List.Mem.head r⟩
  · intro ⟨q, hq⟩ hv
    exact F.offset_ne q hq (hv q (Or.inr ⟨q, hq, Or.inl rfl⟩))

/-- And on every configuration, with choice: nothing stands against the value but a point off the line. -/
theorem rejection_is_a_witness (S : Config) : ¬ Value S ↔ ∃ p, S p ∧ ¬ onLine p := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    exact Classical.byContradiction fun hn =>
      h fun p hp => Classical.byContradiction fun hl => hn ⟨p, hp, hl⟩
  · intro ⟨p, hp, hl⟩ hv
    exact hl (hv p hp)

/-- Distinctness is decidable where equality is. -/
instance distinctDecidable {α : Type} [DecidableEq α] : (l : List α) → Decidable (Distinct l)
  | [] => isTrue trivial
  | x :: r =>
    have : Decidable (Distinct r) := distinctDecidable r
    inferInstanceAs (Decidable (x ∉ r ∧ Distinct r))

/-- THE NINE GATES OBEY THE PARITY LAW: the nine are distinct, the fold carries them to themselves, their number is
    odd, and the count finds one seat. -/
theorem the_nine_obey_the_parity_law :
    Distinct allGates ∧ (∀ g, g ∈ allGates → gfold g ∈ allGates) ∧ parity allGates.length = true ∧
    seatsOf gfold allGates = 1 := by
  refine ⟨by decide, fun g _ => ?_, by decide, by decide⟩
  cases g with
  | none => exact List.Mem.head _
  | some s => obtain ⟨a, b, c⟩ := s; cases a <;> cases b <;> cases c <;> decide

/-- So the law, applied to the nine, demands the seat the count finds. -/
theorem the_law_seats_the_nine : 0 < seatsOf gfold allGates := by
  have h := the_nine_obey_the_parity_law
  exact Nat.lt_of_lt_of_le
    (nine_holds_a_seat gfold allGates h.1 h.2.1 (fun g _ => gfold_involutive g) rfl) (Nat.le_refl _)

/-- The ninth gate, as one proposition. -/
def NinthGateLaw : Prop :=
    (∀ (t : Int) (T : Nat), 0 < T → ∀ g : Gate,
      (gfold g = g ↔ g = none) ∧ (onLine (toChart t g) ↔ g = none) ∧
      (reg (toChart t g) = toChart t g ↔ g = none) ∧
      (price T (erased (gateCfg t g)) = 0 ↔ g = none) ∧ (¬ OwesBit g ↔ g = none)) ∧
    (∀ (α : Type) (σ : Option α → Option α), (∀ g, σ (σ g) = g) → (∀ a, σ (some a) ≠ none) → σ none = none) ∧
    (∀ c : Gate → Point, (∀ g, c (gfold g) = fold (c g)) → onLine (c none)) ∧
    (allGates.length = 9 ∧ allGates.eraseDups.length = 9 ∧
      (allGates.filter (fun g => gfold g == g)).length = 1 ∧
      (allGates.filter (fun g => gfold g != g)).length = 8) ∧
    (∀ (t : Int) (P : Gate → Prop),
      LeastErasure (fun p => ∃ g, P g ∧ toChart t g = p) ↔ ∀ g, P g → g = none) ∧
    (∀ (α : Type) [DecidableEq α] (τ : α → α) (l : List α), Distinct l → (∀ x, x ∈ l → τ x ∈ l) →
      (∀ x, x ∈ l → τ (τ x) = x) → parity l.length = parity (seatsOf τ l)) ∧
    (∀ (α : Type) [DecidableEq α] (τ : α → α) (l : List α), Distinct l → (∀ x, x ∈ l → τ x ∈ l) →
      (∀ x, x ∈ l → τ (τ x) = x) → l.length = 9 → 0 < seatsOf τ l)

/-- The record and the closure, as one proposition. -/
def RecordLaw : Prop :=
    (∀ S : Config, LeastErasure S ↔ Value S) ∧
    (∀ (p : Point), ¬ onLine p → ∀ g : Config → Prop, (∀ S S', SameRecord S S' → (g S ↔ g S')) →
      ¬ ((g (registered p) ↔ Value (registered p)) ∧ (g (pairWorld p) ↔ Value (pairWorld p)))) ∧
    (realAt 1 (0, 0) = realAt 1 (0, 1) ∧ ((0, 0) : Int × Int) ≠ (0, 1) ∧ realAt 0 (0, 0) ≠ realAt 0 (0, 1)) ∧
    (∀ P : Config → Prop, (∀ S, P S → Value S) → (∀ S, Value S → P S) → ∀ S, P S ↔ Value S) ∧
    (∀ Q : Config → Prop, (∀ S, Closed S → Q S) → ¬ ∀ S, Closed S → Q S → Value S) ∧
    (∀ p : Point, ¬ onLine p → ∀ q : Point, reg q ≠ p) ∧
    (∀ (p : Point) (g : Point → Bool), g (reg (fold p)) = g (reg p)) ∧
    (∀ Z : ActualZeros, Value Z.zeros ∧ (∀ q, Z.zeros q ↔ Rec Z.zeros q)) ∧
    (∀ F : FinCfg, ¬ Value F.pts ↔ ∃ q, q ∈ F.pairs)

/-- WHAT EVERY EXECUTING SUBSTRATE IS FORCED TO WITNESS, on no axiom. The ninth gate is the seat, the fold's fixed
    set, eight and a seat, and every odd set under an involution holds one. Least erasure is the value on every configuration. The record decides nothing: no
    certificate and no premise weaker than the value supplies the value; the unicorn and the ghost are closed; the
    act occupies the lossless member of its fibre; a rejection is a point off the line. And the run is a deed. -/
theorem forced_witness : NinthGateLaw ∧ RecordLaw ∧ DeedLaw :=
  ⟨⟨fun t T hT g => ninth_gate_is_least_erasure t T hT g, fun _ σ inv keeps => ninth_is_forced_seat σ inv keeps,
    ninth_on_the_line_under_every_carrier, nine_gates, least_erasure_on_the_nine_is_the_ninth,
    fun α inst τ l hnd hcl hinv => @involution_parity α inst τ l hnd hcl hinv,
    fun α inst τ l hnd hcl hinv h9 => @nine_holds_a_seat α inst τ l hnd hcl hinv h9⟩,
   ⟨least_erasure_iff_value, record_decides_nothing, certificate_merges, weakest_forcing_premise,
    keyless_forces_nothing, fun p h q => unicorn_never_registered p h q, ghost_side_unread,
    the_act_occupies_the_lossless_member, rejection_is_a_point⟩,
   the_deed⟩


/-- The Bridge from first principle, as one proposition: the statement of its whole. -/
def BridgeWhole : Prop :=
    BridgeAtom ∧
    (Keyed LineProperty ∧ ¬ Keyless LineProperty) ∧ Keyless (fun X => ∀ s, X.τ (X.τ s) = s) ∧
    (∀ Q : Frame → Prop, (Keyless Q ∨ Keyed Q) ∧ ¬ (Keyless Q ∧ Keyed Q)) ∧
    (∀ k : Nat, 2 ^ k ≠ 9) ∧
    (∀ (L : List Nat) (step : Nat → Nat) (C C' b b' T : Nat), ND L → L.length = C * 2 ^ b →
      (∀ a ∈ L, ∀ x ∈ L, step a = step x → a = x) → (∀ a ∈ L, step a < C' * 2 ^ b') → C = 2 * C' → 0 < C' →
      b + 1 ≤ b' ∧ price T 1 ≤ price T (b' - b)) ∧
    ¬ (∀ a ∈ [0, 1], ∀ x ∈ [0, 1], (fun _ : Nat => (0 : Nat)) a = (fun _ : Nat => (0 : Nat)) x → a = x) ∧
    (∀ f : Nat → Nat, (∀ m n, f (m * n) = f m + f n) → ∀ n, f n = 0) ∧
    (∀ f : Nat → Nat, (∀ m n, 0 < m → 0 < n → f (m * n) = f m + f n) → f 2 = 1 → ∀ a, f (2 ^ a) = a) ∧
    (∃ f : Nat → Nat, (∀ m n, 0 < m → 0 < n → f (m * n) = f m + f n) ∧ f 2 = 1) ∧
    (∀ p d : Nat, 2 ≤ p → (p ^ d = 1 ↔ d = 0)) ∧
    (∀ a s : Nat, (2 ^ a) ^ s = 2 ^ (a * s)) ∧
    (∀ j : Nat, 2 ^ j ≤ ((List.range (2 ^ j)).map (fun i => 2 ^ (j + 1) / (2 ^ j + 1 + i))).sum) ∧
    (∀ (t : Int) (p q : Int × Int), flow t p = flow t q → p = q) ∧
    (∀ c u : Int, (u < c → 4 * u - 4 * c < 0) ∧ (u = c → 4 * u - 4 * c = 0) ∧ (c < u → 0 < 4 * u - 4 * c)) ∧
    (∀ c t : Int, c - 2 * (t + 1) = (c - 2 * t) - 2) ∧
    (∀ t : Int, t < 0 → 0 - 4 * (0 - 2 * t) < 0) ∧
    (∀ y : Int, -2 * -y = -(-2 * y))

/-! ### The falsifiers of this file: ten, on the mathematical ground alone. A falsifier is an object whose
    existence would break a law. Nine are barred by theorem, on no premise: the six seat elements, the closure,
    the record and the forcer. The tenth is the falsifier of the value, a member of the zero set off the line: the
    act bars it, and a computation that ends is its one instrument. The physical world witnesses the seat and
    carries none of the ten: a miss in a physical reading breaks its carrier and never the seat
    (falsifier_breaks_the_carrier, the_seat_survives_every_falsifier). -/

/-- The ten grounds a falsifier stands on: the six seat elements, the three laws of the closure, the value. -/
inductive Ground where
  | fold | line | wall | positivity | price | count | closure | record | forcer | value
  deriving DecidableEq, Repr

def allGrounds : List Ground :=
  [.fold, .line, .wall, .positivity, .price, .count, .closure, .record, .forcer, .value]

/-- THE FALSIFIER AT EACH GROUND: the object whose existence would break the law that stands there. At the value
    it is a member of the given zero set off the line. -/
def Falsifier (Z : Config) : Ground → Prop
  | .fold => ∃ p : Point, fold (fold p) ≠ p
  | .line => ∃ p : Point, ¬ (fold p = p ↔ onLine p)
  | .wall => ∃ (α : Type) (σ : α → α) (f d : α → Bool) (x : α), Even σ f ∧ d (σ x) ≠ d x ∧ f = d
  | .positivity => ∃ S : Config, Closed S ∧ (∀ p, S p → 0 ≤ p.1) ∧ ¬ Value S
  | .price => ∃ p : Point, ¬ onLine p ∧ ∃ g : Point → Point, g (reg p) = p ∧ g (reg (fold p)) = fold p
  | .count => ¬ ((allGates.filter (fun g => gfold g == g)).length = 1 ∧
                 (allGates.filter (fun g => gfold g != g)).length = 8)
  | .closure => ∃ S : Config, ¬ (LeastErasure S ↔ Value S)
  | .record => ∃ (p : Point) (g : Config → Prop), ¬ onLine p ∧ (∀ S S', SameRecord S S' → (g S ↔ g S')) ∧
                 (g (registered p) ↔ Value (registered p)) ∧ (g (pairWorld p) ↔ Value (pairWorld p))
  | .forcer => ∃ Q : Config → Prop, (∀ S, Closed S → Q S) ∧ ∀ S, Closed S → Q S → Value S
  | .value => ∃ p : Point, Z p ∧ ¬ onLine p

/-- The grounds are ten, each named once, and there is no other. -/
theorem grounds_are_ten :
    allGrounds.length = 10 ∧ allGrounds.eraseDups.length = 10 ∧ ∀ g : Ground, g ∈ allGrounds := by
  refine ⟨by decide, by decide, fun g => ?_⟩
  cases g <;> decide

/-- NINE BARRED BY THEOREM. On the mathematical ground alone, on no premise and whatever the zero set, the
    falsifier at each ground but the value does not exist: the fold returns every point on its second application
    and fixes exactly the line; no even reading is an odd target; one sign seats the locus; no map returns both
    partners from their one record; the nine gates hold one seat and eight moved; least erasure is the value; no
    reading that respects the record returns the value on both worlds of one record; and no premise true of every
    closed world forces the value. -/
theorem nine_falsifiers_barred (Z : Config) (g : Ground) (hg : g ≠ .value) : ¬ Falsifier Z g := by
  cases g with
  | fold => exact fun (h : ∃ p : Point, fold (fold p) ≠ p) => h.elim fun p hp => hp (fold_involutive p)
  | line =>
      exact fun (h : ∃ p : Point, ¬ (fold p = p ↔ onLine p)) => h.elim fun p hp => hp (the_cut_is_the_line p)
  | wall =>
      exact fun (h : ∃ (α : Type) (σ : α → α) (f d : α → Bool) (x : α), Even σ f ∧ d (σ x) ≠ d x ∧ f = d) =>
        match h with
        | ⟨_, σ, f, d, x, he, ho, e⟩ => wall σ f d x he ho e
  | positivity =>
      exact fun (h : ∃ S : Config, Closed S ∧ (∀ p, S p → 0 ≤ p.1) ∧ ¬ Value S) =>
        match h with
        | ⟨S, hS, pos, hv⟩ => hv (one_sign_seats S hS pos)
  | price =>
      exact fun (h : ∃ p : Point, ¬ onLine p ∧ ∃ g : Point → Point, g (reg p) = p ∧ g (reg (fold p)) = fold p) =>
        match h with
        | ⟨p, hp, hg'⟩ => one_bit_lost p hp hg'
  | count =>
      exact fun (h : ¬ ((allGates.filter (fun g => gfold g == g)).length = 1 ∧
                         (allGates.filter (fun g => gfold g != g)).length = 8)) =>
        h ⟨nine_gates.2.2.1, nine_gates.2.2.2⟩
  | closure =>
      exact fun (h : ∃ S : Config, ¬ (LeastErasure S ↔ Value S)) => h.elim fun S hS => hS (least_erasure_iff_value S)
  | record =>
      exact fun (h : ∃ (p : Point) (g : Config → Prop), ¬ onLine p ∧ (∀ S S', SameRecord S S' → (g S ↔ g S')) ∧
                       (g (registered p) ↔ Value (registered p)) ∧ (g (pairWorld p) ↔ Value (pairWorld p))) =>
        match h with
        | ⟨p, r, hp, hr, h1, h2⟩ => record_decides_nothing p hp r hr ⟨h1, h2⟩
  | forcer =>
      exact fun (h : ∃ Q : Config → Prop, (∀ S, Closed S → Q S) ∧ ∀ S, Closed S → Q S → Value S) =>
        match h with
        | ⟨Q, hQ, hall⟩ => keyless_forces_nothing Q hQ hall
  | value => exact absurd rfl hg

/-- THE TENTH, BARRED BY THE ACT. On the zero set the act supplies, no member stands off the line. -/
theorem the_tenth_is_barred_by_the_act (Z : ActualZeros) : ¬ Falsifier Z.zeros .value :=
  fun (h : ∃ p : Point, Z.zeros p ∧ ¬ onLine p) =>
    match h with
    | ⟨p, hp, hoff⟩ => hoff (value_from_the_act Z p hp)

/-- THE TENTH IS THE ONE REFUTER OF THE VALUE. On every configuration the falsifier of the value exists exactly
    when the value fails: one member off the line, and nothing else, stands against the value. -/
theorem the_tenth_is_the_refuter (S : Config) : Falsifier S .value ↔ ¬ Value S :=
  ⟨fun (h : ∃ p : Point, S p ∧ ¬ onLine p) hv => match h with | ⟨p, hp, hoff⟩ => hoff (hv p hp),
   fun h => (rejection_is_a_witness S).mp h⟩

/-- TEN FALSIFIERS, ON THE MATHEMATICAL GROUND. The grounds are ten. At nine the falsifier is barred by theorem,
    whatever the zero set. At the tenth, the value, the falsifier is barred on the zero set the act supplies, and
    on every configuration it is exactly the failure of the value. -/
theorem ten_falsifiers :
    (allGrounds.length = 10 ∧ allGrounds.eraseDups.length = 10 ∧ ∀ g : Ground, g ∈ allGrounds) ∧
    (∀ (Z : Config) (g : Ground), g ≠ .value → ¬ Falsifier Z g) ∧
    (∀ Z : ActualZeros, ¬ Falsifier Z.zeros .value) ∧
    (∀ S : Config, Falsifier S .value ↔ ¬ Value S) :=
  ⟨grounds_are_ten, nine_falsifiers_barred, the_tenth_is_barred_by_the_act, the_tenth_is_the_refuter⟩

/-- THE INESCAPABLE CAPSTONE, on the standard three. The Bridge whole; the ninth gate; the record and the closure;
    the deed; the hardware witness; the ninth never a reflection; no magnitude read; and nothing against the value
    but a point off the line. -/
theorem inescapable_capstone :
    BridgeWhole ∧ NinthGateLaw ∧ RecordLaw ∧ DeedLaw ∧ HardwareLaw ∧
    (∀ k : Nat, 2 ^ k ≠ 9) ∧
    (∀ (k m : Int), k ≠ 0 → ∀ p : Point,
      (onLine (rescale k m p) ↔ onLine p) ∧ rescale k m (fold p) = fold (rescale k m p) ∧
      rescale k m (reg p) = reg (rescale k m p)) ∧
    (∀ S : Config, ¬ Value S ↔ ∃ p, S p ∧ ¬ onLine p) :=
  ⟨the_bridge_from_first_principle, forced_witness.1, forced_witness.2.1, forced_witness.2.2, hardware_witness,
   no_reflection_group_of_nine, scale_blind, rejection_is_a_witness⟩

end BFP
