### RH_Seal_Twin.f90

~~~~~fortran file=RH_Seal_Twin.f90
! RH_Seal_Twin.f90 · twin of PhysOS Proof PSP-RH-SEAL-01, the terminal seal at least erasure, executed.
! Build (sealed): gfortran -std=f2018 -O2 -fno-fast-math -ffp-contract=off RH_Seal_Twin.f90
! The chart at resolution ten: x = 20 Re s, line x = 10, fold x -> 20 - x. A world is a fold-closed set of real parts
! at one height; its record is its registration onto the line; least erasure is read from its definition.
program rh_seal_twin
  implicit none
  integer, parameter :: i16 = selected_int_kind(38)
  integer :: checks, fails, m, n, i, nw, nag, nrej, nprice, nact, nsep, nroot, nctl
  logical :: le, lec
  checks = 0; fails = 0; nw = 0; nag = 0; nrej = 0; nprice = 0; nact = 0; nsep = 0; nroot = 0; nctl = 0
  do m = 0, 2**19 - 1
    if (.not. sym(m)) cycle
    nw = nw + 1
    le = .true.
    if (erases(m)) then
      do n = 0, 2**19 - 1
        if (sym(n) .and. ((n /= 0) .eqv. (m /= 0)) .and. .not. erases(n)) le = .false.
      end do
    end if
    ! control: the line removed from the universe. Among worlds that hold no point on the line an erasing world has
    ! no rival of its record that erases nothing, so least erasure by its definition parts from the value.
    if (.not. btest(m, 9)) then
      lec = .true.
      if (erases(m)) then
        do n = 0, 2**19 - 1
          if (sym(n) .and. .not. btest(n, 9) .and. ((n /= 0) .eqv. (m /= 0)) .and. .not. erases(n)) lec = .false.
        end do
      end if
      if (lec .neqv. rh(m)) nctl = nctl + 1
    end if
    if (le .eqv. rh(m)) nag = nag + 1
    if ((.not. le) .eqv. erases(m)) nrej = nrej + 1
    if ((offcount(m) == 0) .eqv. le) nprice = nprice + 1
    if ((.not. le) .or. rh(m)) nact = nact + 1
    if (m /= 0 .and. m /= ibset(0, 9) .and. .not. le) nsep = nsep + 1
    if (rh(m)) nroot = ior(nroot, 1)
    if (.not. rh(m)) nroot = ior(nroot, 2)
  end do
  call check('1024 fold-closed worlds at one height', nw == 1024)
  call check('least erasure is the value on every world', nag == 1024)
  call check('control, the line removed from the universe: least erasure parts from the value on 511 worlds', nctl == 511)
  call check('a rejection of least erasure is exactly a point off the line', nrej == 1024)
  call check('the price is zero exactly at least erasure, one bit per point off the line', nprice == 1024)
  call check('the act carries the value: every least-erasure world satisfies the hypothesis', nact == 1024)
  call check('the bit is keyed: worlds of one record differ in least erasure', nsep > 0)
  call check('the root crosses neither way: a property true on every world holds on both sides', nroot == 3)
  call check('the floor exact: 1380649 x 300 x 6931471805599453 = 2870978885078723755499100', &
       1380649_i16 * 300_i16 * 6931471805599453_i16 == 2870978885078723755499100_i16)
  write(*,'(a,i0,a,i0,a)') ' BATTERY-JSON: {"checks":', checks, ',"failures":', fails, '}'
  if (fails > 0) error stop 1
contains
  pure logical function sym(m)
    integer, intent(in) :: m
    integer :: i
    sym = .true.
    do i = 1, 19
      if (btest(m, i-1) .neqv. btest(m, 19-i)) sym = .false.
    end do
  end function sym
  pure integer function offcount(m)
    integer, intent(in) :: m
    integer :: i
    offcount = 0
    do i = 1, 19
      if (btest(m, i-1) .and. i /= 10) offcount = offcount + 1
    end do
  end function offcount
  pure logical function erases(m)
    integer, intent(in) :: m
    erases = offcount(m) > 0
  end function erases
  pure logical function rh(m)
    integer, intent(in) :: m
    rh = offcount(m) == 0
  end function rh
  subroutine check(name, ok)
    character(*), intent(in) :: name
    logical, intent(in) :: ok
    checks = checks + 1
    if (.not. ok) fails = fails + 1
    write(*,'(a,a)') merge('  PASS  ','  FAIL  ',ok), name
  end subroutine check
end program rh_seal_twin
~~~~~

### Inescapable_Twin.f90

~~~~~fortran file=Inescapable_Twin.f90
! Inescapable_Twin.f90 . the executed twin of Inescapable_Capstone.lean, PhysOS Proof PSP-CAPSTONE-01.
! 0 to VII are the twin of The Bridge From First Principle, edition 1.0.0, carried whole; VIII the parity law
! and the ninth gate, IX the hardware witness, X the deed and XI the closure are added. Every check is a
! finite computation that ends. No named human result is a premise.
! Build (sealed): gfortran -std=f2018 -O2 -fno-fast-math -ffp-contract=off
program inescapable_twin
  use, intrinsic :: iso_fortran_env, only: dp => real64, i8 => int64
  implicit none
  integer :: nchk = 0, nfail = 0
  call conduct()
  call atom()
  call three_twelve_eight()
  call pay()
  call supply()
  call primes()
  call wall_edge_seat()
  call heat_flow()
  call ninth_gate()
  call hardware()
  call deed()
  call closure()
  write(*,'(a,i0,a,i0,a)') ' BATTERY-JSON: {"checks":', nchk, ',"failures":', nfail, '}'
  if (nfail /= 0) error stop 1
contains
  subroutine check(name, ok)
    character(*), intent(in) :: name
    logical, intent(in) :: ok
    nchk = nchk + 1
    if (.not. ok) nfail = nfail + 1
    write(*,'(a,a)') merge('  PASS  ','  FAIL  ', ok), name
  end subroutine check

  ! 0 . conduct: the arithmetic this twin runs on is the arithmetic it claims
  subroutine conduct()
    real(dp), volatile :: one, x, y, r, z
    one = 1.0_dp
    x = one + scale(one, -30); y = one - scale(one, -30)
    r = x*y - one
    z = ieee_nan()
    write(*,'(a)') '0 CONDUCT'
    call check('0: no fused multiply-add executed (a fused path reads -2^-60)', abs(r) <= 0.0_dp)
    call check('0: NaN is ordered against nothing, itself included', .not. (z <= z .or. z > z))
  end subroutine conduct
  function ieee_nan() result(z)
    use, intrinsic :: ieee_arithmetic, only: ieee_value, ieee_quiet_nan
    real(dp) :: z
    z = ieee_value(1.0_dp, ieee_quiet_nan)
  end function ieee_nan

  ! I . the atom on a window: fold, line, registration, the lost bit, least erasure equal to the value
  pure function foldp(p) result(q)
    integer, intent(in) :: p(2)
    integer :: q(2)
    q = [-p(1), p(2)]
  end function foldp
  pure function regp(p) result(q)
    integer, intent(in) :: p(2)
    integer :: q(2)
    q = [0, p(2)]
  end function regp
  subroutine atom()
    integer :: d, t, k, m, g1, g2, g3, h, nboth, none_
    integer :: got, best, bestc, nbc, nsame, q1(2), r1(2), r2(2)
    integer :: g(0:2), pd(9), pt(9), p(2)
    logical :: ok1, ok2, ok3, le, va
    write(*,'(a)') 'I THE ATOM'
    ok1 = .true.; ok2 = .true.; ok3 = .true.
    do d = -50, 50
      do t = -5, 5
        p = [d, t]
        if (any(foldp(foldp(p)) /= p)) ok1 = .false.
        if (all(foldp(p) == p) .neqv. (d == 0)) ok1 = .false.
        if (all(regp(p) == p) .neqv. (d == 0)) ok2 = .false.
        if (any(regp(p) /= [0, t])) ok2 = .false.
        if (d /= 0) then
          if (all(foldp(p) == p)) ok3 = .false.
          if (any(regp(foldp(p)) /= regp(p))) ok3 = .false.
        end if
      end do
    end do
    call check('I: the fold undoes itself and fixes exactly the line, 1111 points', ok1)
    call check('I: the registration lands on the line, keeps the height, erases nothing exactly on it', ok2)
    call check('I: every off-line point has a distinct partner of one record, 1100 points', ok3)
    ! window: d in {-1,0,1}, t in {0,1,2}; the records are the three heights; 9^3 = 729 maps from records to points
    k = 0
    do t = 0, 2
      do d = -1, 1
        k = k + 1; pd(k) = d; pt(k) = t
      end do
    end do
    nboth = 0; none_ = 0; best = 0
    do g1 = 1, 9
      do g2 = 1, 9
        do g3 = 1, 9
          g = [g1, g2, g3]
          do h = 0, 2
            ! the pair at height h is (1,h) and its fold partner; the record of each is computed by the registration
            ! and the map is read at each record: the members it returns of the pair number 0, 1 or 2
            q1 = [1, h]; r1 = regp(q1); r2 = regp(foldp(q1))
            got = 0
            m = g(r1(2))
            if (pd(m) == 1 .and. pt(m) == h) got = got + 1
            m = g(r2(2))
            if (pd(m) == -1 .and. pt(m) == h) got = got + 1
            best = max(best, got)
            if (got == 1) none_ = none_ + 1
            if (got == 2) nboth = nboth + 1
          end do
        end do
      end do
    end do
    ! what can fail is checked: the partners of each pair are distinct and the registration, computed, sends both
    ! to one record; that no map returns both is then the consequence, printed and no pass condition
    nsame = 0
    do h = 0, 2
      q1 = [1, h]; r1 = regp(q1); r2 = regp(foldp(q1))
      if (all(r1 == r2) .and. any(q1 /= foldp(q1))) nsame = nsame + 1
    end do
    write(*,'(a,i0,a,i0,a,i0,a,i0)') '  pairs sent to one record ', nsame, ' of 3; most recovered of a pair ', best, &
         '; one member ', none_, ' times; both, the consequence, ', nboth
    call check('I: both partners of each pair go to one record; the most any map recovers of a pair is one member', &
         nsame == 3 .and. best == 1 .and. none_ == 486)
    bestc = 0; nbc = 0
    do g1 = 1, 3
      do g2 = 1, 3
        do g3 = 1, 3
          ! control: a registration that keeps the side, at one height: the records are the three points themselves
          got = 0
          if (g3 == 3) got = got + 1
          if (g1 == 1) got = got + 1
          bestc = max(bestc, got)
          if (got == 2) nbc = nbc + 1
        end do
      end do
    end do
    call check('I: control, a registration that keeps the side: three maps recover both members', bestc == 2 .and. nbc == 3)
    ! least erasure, read through the registration, against the value, read through the offset
    ok1 = .true.
    do m = 0, 4095
      le = .true.; va = .true.
      do k = 0, 11
        if (btest(m, k)) then
          p = [mod(k, 3) - 1, k / 3]
          if (any(regp(p) /= p)) le = .false.
          if (p(1) /= 0) va = .false.
        end if
      end do
      if (le .neqv. va) ok1 = .false.
    end do
    call check('I: least erasure equals the value on all 4096 subsets of twelve points', ok1)
  end subroutine atom

  ! II . three, twelve, eight, the ninth
  subroutine three_twelve_eight()
    integer :: m, t, v, cnt, nlock, a, b, c, i, j, n, nperm, ninv, s, ok_cnt
    integer :: r(3,3), perm(4), even_perms(4,12)
    logical :: ok, used(4)
    write(*,'(a)') 'II THREE, TWELVE, EIGHT, THE NINTH'
    ok = .true.
    do m = 0, 63
      do t = 0, 3
        cnt = 0
        do v = 0, 7
          if (mod(rowdot(m/8, v), 2) == t/2 .and. mod(rowdot(mod(m,8), v), 2) == mod(t,2)) cnt = cnt + 1
        end do
        if (cnt == 1) ok = .false.
      end do
    end do
    call check('II: no two-axis system over GF(2) has exactly one solution, 256 systems', ok)
    nlock = 0; ok = .true.
    do m = 0, 511
      do i = 1, 3
        r(i,1) = mod(ishft(m, -(3*(3-i)+2)), 2); r(i,2) = mod(ishft(m, -(3*(3-i)+1)), 2)
        r(i,3) = mod(ishft(m, -(3*(3-i))), 2)
      end do
      if (det2(r) == 1) then
        nlock = nlock + 1
        do t = 0, 7
          cnt = 0
          do v = 0, 7
            if (mod(r(1,1)*bit(v,2)+r(1,2)*bit(v,1)+r(1,3)*bit(v,0),2) == bit(t,2) .and. &
                mod(r(2,1)*bit(v,2)+r(2,2)*bit(v,1)+r(2,3)*bit(v,0),2) == bit(t,1) .and. &
                mod(r(3,1)*bit(v,2)+r(3,2)*bit(v,1)+r(3,3)*bit(v,0),2) == bit(t,0)) cnt = cnt + 1
          end do
          if (cnt /= 1) ok = .false.
        end do
      end if
    end do
    call check('II: 168 three-axis systems have determinant one and each locks all eight targets', nlock == 168 .and. ok)
    ! twelve: even permutations of four, acting on the twelve directed gates
    nperm = 0
    do a = 1, 4
      do b = 1, 4
        do c = 1, 4
          do s = 1, 4
            perm = [a, b, c, s]
            used = .false.; ok = .true.
            do i = 1, 4
              if (used(perm(i))) ok = .false.
              used(perm(i)) = .true.
            end do
            if (.not. ok) cycle
            ninv = 0
            do i = 1, 3
              do j = i+1, 4
                if (perm(i) > perm(j)) ninv = ninv + 1
              end do
            end do
            if (mod(ninv, 2) == 0) then
              nperm = nperm + 1; even_perms(:, nperm) = perm
            end if
          end do
        end do
      end do
    end do
    ok = (nperm == 12)
    do a = 1, 4
      do b = 1, 4
        if (a == b) cycle
        do c = 1, 4
          do s = 1, 4
            if (c == s) cycle
            ok_cnt = 0
            do n = 1, nperm
              if (even_perms(a, n) == c .and. even_perms(b, n) == s) ok_cnt = ok_cnt + 1
            end do
            if (ok_cnt /= 1) ok = .false.
          end do
        end do
      end do
    end do
    call check('II: twelve rotations, and exactly one carries any directed gate to any directed gate', ok)
    ! eight: sign patterns, total negation free, orientation flipped
    ok = .true.
    do m = 0, 7
      if (ieor(m, 7) == m) ok = .false.
      if (mod(popcnt(m) + popcnt(ieor(m, 7)), 2) /= 1) ok = .false.
    end do
    call check('II: eight patterns, total negation moves each and joins an even to an odd', ok)
    ! the ninth: 2^k is never 9, and every odd fibre holds exactly one seat
    ok = .true.
    do i = 0, 62
      if (2_i8**i == 9_i8) ok = .false.
    end do
    call check('II: 2^k is never nine, k = 0..62', ok)
  end subroutine three_twelve_eight
  integer function rowdot(rr, v)
    integer, intent(in) :: rr, v
    rowdot = bit(rr,2)*bit(v,2) + bit(rr,1)*bit(v,1) + bit(rr,0)*bit(v,0)
  end function rowdot
  integer function bit(x, k)
    integer, intent(in) :: x, k
    bit = mod(ishft(x, -k), 2)
  end function bit
  integer function det2(r)
    integer, intent(in) :: r(3,3)
    det2 = mod(r(1,1)*(r(2,2)*r(3,3)+r(2,3)*r(3,2)) + r(1,2)*(r(2,1)*r(3,3)+r(2,3)*r(3,1)) + &
               r(1,3)*(r(2,1)*r(3,2)+r(2,2)*r(3,1)), 2)
  end function det2

  ! III . pay: pigeonhole and the export, exhaustively on small wholes
  logical function injective_exists(n, m)
    integer, intent(in) :: n, m
    integer :: f(8), i, j
    logical :: inj
    integer(i8) :: code, total, cc
    injective_exists = .false.
    total = int(m, i8)**n
    do code = 0_i8, total - 1_i8
      cc = code
      do i = 1, n
        f(i) = int(mod(cc, int(m, i8))); cc = cc / int(m, i8)
      end do
      inj = .true.
      do i = 1, n - 1
        do j = i + 1, n
          if (f(i) == f(j)) inj = .false.
        end do
      end do
      if (inj) then
        injective_exists = .true.; return
      end if
    end do
  end function injective_exists
  subroutine pay()
    integer :: n, m, cp, f, fp, k
    integer, parameter :: cps(5) = [1, 1, 1, 2, 3], fs(5) = [1, 2, 3, 1, 1], fpmax(5) = [10, 8, 8, 8, 3]
    logical :: ok
    integer(i8) :: a, b
    write(*,'(a)') 'III PAY'
    ok = .true.
    do n = 1, 6
      do m = 1, 6
        if (injective_exists(n, m) .neqv. (n <= m)) ok = .false.
      end do
    end do
    call check('III: n distinct states fit injectively in m cells exactly when n <= m, every n, m <= 6', ok)
    ok = .true.
    do k = 1, 5
      cp = cps(k); f = fs(k)
      do fp = 1, fpmax(k)
        n = 2*cp*f; m = cp*fp
        if (injective_exists(n, m) .neqv. (2*f <= fp)) ok = .false.
      end do
    end do
    call check('III: the content halves and nothing merges exactly when the freedom at least doubles', ok)
    call check('III: a merging step halves the content with no freedom exported (two states, one cell)', &
         .not. injective_exists(2, 1))
    ok = .true.
    do a = 1_i8, 300_i8
      do b = 1_i8, 300_i8
        if (v2(a*b) /= v2(a) + v2(b)) ok = .false.
      end do
    end do
    call check('III: the two-adic valuation is additive on positive arguments, 90000 pairs', ok .and. v2(2_i8) == 1)
  end subroutine pay
  integer function v2(x)
    integer(i8), intent(in) :: x
    integer(i8) :: y
    v2 = 0; y = x
    do while (mod(y, 2_i8) == 0_i8)
      v2 = v2 + 1; y = y / 2_i8
    end do
  end function v2

  ! IV . supply: the calibration is unique, and no reading of the content returns the deed
  subroutine supply()
    integer :: sx, dx, c, ncal, gcode, q, nret
    logical :: ok, all_match
    write(*,'(a)') 'IV SUPPLY'
    ok = .true.
    do sx = 0, 1
      do dx = 0, 1
        ncal = 0
        do c = 0, 1
          ! on the orbit {x, sigma x}: d(x) = s(x) xor c and d(sigma x) = s(sigma x) xor c, with s, d odd
          if (dx == ieor(sx, c) .and. 1 - dx == ieor(1 - sx, c)) ncal = ncal + 1
        end do
        if (ncal /= 1) ok = .false.
      end do
    end do
    call check('IV: for every odd witness and odd target, exactly one calibration bit', ok)
    nret = 0
    do gcode = 0, 7
      all_match = .true.
      do q = 0, 2
        ! a reading of the content q must equal ran on the executed state (1, q) and on the unexecuted (0, q)
        if (bit(gcode, q) /= 1) all_match = .false.
        if (bit(gcode, q) /= 0) all_match = .false.
      end do
      if (all_match) nret = nret + 1
    end do
    call check('IV: of the 8 readings of a three-element content, none returns whether it ran', nret == 0)
  end subroutine supply

  ! V . primes: one free orbit, the parity frame, the divisor cube, the balance
  subroutine primes()
    integer, parameter :: N = 1000000
    integer, allocatable :: dc(:), acc(:), mu(:)
    logical, allocatable :: comp(:)
    integer :: d, m, r, k, nsq
    logical :: ok_odd, ok_bal, ok_prime, ok_k4, ok_seat
    integer, parameter :: kp(6) = [11, 13, 17, 19, 23, 29], ks(6) = [851, 1273, 437, 2119, 1703, 869]
    write(*,'(a)') 'V PRIMES'
    allocate(dc(N), acc(N), mu(N), comp(N))
    dc = 0; acc = 0; mu = 1; comp = .false.
    do d = 2, N
      if (.not. comp(d)) then
        do m = 2*d, N, d
          comp(m) = .true.
        end do
        do m = d, N, d
          mu(m) = -mu(m)
        end do
        if (int(d,i8)*int(d,i8) <= int(N,i8)) then
          do m = d*d, N, d*d
            mu(m) = 0
          end do
        end if
      end if
    end do
    do d = 1, N
      do m = d, N, d
        dc(m) = dc(m) + 1
        acc(m) = acc(m) + mu(d)
      end do
    end do
    ok_odd = .true.; ok_bal = .true.; ok_prime = .true.; ok_seat = .true.
    do m = 1, N
      r = int(sqrt(real(m, dp)))
      do while (r*r > m); r = r - 1; end do
      do while ((r+1)*(r+1) <= m); r = r + 1; end do
      nsq = merge(1, 0, r*r == m)
      if (mod(dc(m), 2) /= nsq) ok_odd = .false.
      if (m == 1 .and. acc(m) /= 1) ok_bal = .false.
      if (m > 1 .and. acc(m) /= 0) ok_bal = .false.
      if (m > 1 .and. ((dc(m) == 2) .neqv. (.not. comp(m)))) ok_prime = .false.
      if (m > 1 .and. .not. comp(m) .and. nsq /= 0) ok_seat = .false.
    end do
    call check('V: the fibre is odd exactly when it holds a seat, and holds at most one, n <= 10^6', ok_odd)
    call check('V: a prime is exactly a fibre of one free orbit, with no seat, n <= 10^6', ok_prime .and. ok_seat)
    call check('V: every finite fibre balances, the signs over the divisors sum to [n = 1], n <= 10^6', ok_bal)
    ok_k4 = .true.
    do k = 1, 6
      if (mod(kp(k), 420) /= mod(ks(k), 420)) ok_k4 = .false.
      if (dc(kp(k)) /= 2 .or. dc(ks(k)) /= 4) ok_k4 = .false.
      if (mu(kp(k)) /= -1 .or. mu(ks(k)) /= 1) ok_k4 = .false.
    end do
    call check('V: the parity frame: residues mod 420 merge each pair, the paid bits 1 and 2 separate it', ok_k4)
    call check('V: thirty has the eight divisors of the sign cube, signs four and four', &
         dc(30) == 8 .and. sum(mu([1,2,3,5,6,10,15,30])) == 0)
    deallocate(dc, acc, mu, comp)
  end subroutine primes

  ! VI . wall, edge, seat
  pure function theta(x) result(s)
    real(dp), intent(in) :: x
    real(dp) :: s
    integer :: n
    s = 0.0_dp
    do n = 80, 1, -1
      s = s + exp(-acos(-1.0_dp) * real(n,dp)**2 * x)
    end do
    s = 1.0_dp + 2.0_dp * s
  end function theta
  subroutine wall_edge_seat()
    integer, parameter :: NW = 10000000
    real(dp), parameter :: xs(7) = [0.25_dp, 0.5_dp, 0.8_dp, 1.0_dp, 1.5_dp, 2.0_dp, 4.0_dp]
    real(dp) :: worst, rr, s1, s2, h, best, ratio
    integer(i8) :: n, lo, hi, mm
    integer :: k, j, d, m, xbest
    integer(1), allocatable :: mu(:)
    logical, allocatable :: comp(:)
    logical :: ok1, ok2, ok3
    write(*,'(a)') 'VI WALL, EDGE, SEAT'
    worst = 0.0_dp
    do k = 1, 7
      rr = abs(theta(1.0_dp/xs(k)) - sqrt(xs(k))*theta(xs(k))) / (sqrt(xs(k))*theta(xs(k)))
      worst = max(worst, rr)
    end do
    write(*,'(a,es10.3)') '  theta(1/x) against sqrt(x) theta(x), worst relative gap over seven scales: ', worst
    call check('VI: the lattice sum is self-dual; its weight is the square root, the fold''s centre', worst < 1.0e-13_dp)
    ok1 = .true.; ok2 = .true.; ok3 = .true.; h = 1.0_dp
    do j = 0, 24
      lo = 2_i8**j + 1_i8; hi = 2_i8**(j+1)
      s1 = 0.0_dp; s2 = 0.0_dp
      do n = hi, lo, -1
        s1 = s1 + 1.0_dp/real(n,dp)
        s2 = s2 + 1.0_dp/real(n,dp)**2
      end do
      h = h + s1
      if (s1 < 0.5_dp .or. s1 > 1.0_dp) ok1 = .false.
      if (s2 > 2.0_dp**(-j)) ok2 = .false.
      if (h < 1.0_dp + 0.5_dp*real(j+1,dp)) ok3 = .false.
    end do
    call check('VI: every block of shares one-in-n holds between a half and one: the wall at Re s = 1', ok1 .and. ok3)
    call check('VI: at two units per bit every block holds at most 2^-j: finite past the wall', ok2)
    allocate(mu(NW), comp(NW))
    mu = 1_1; comp = .false.
    do d = 2, NW
      if (.not. comp(d)) then
        do m = 2*d, NW, d
          comp(m) = .true.
        end do
        do m = d, NW, d
          mu(m) = -mu(m)
        end do
        if (int(d,i8)*int(d,i8) <= int(NW,i8)) then
          do m = d*d, NW, d*d
            mu(m) = 0_1
          end do
        end if
      end if
    end do
    mm = 0_i8; best = 0.0_dp; xbest = 0
    do m = 1, NW
      mm = mm + int(mu(m), i8)
      if (m >= 100) then
        ratio = abs(real(mm,dp)) / sqrt(real(m,dp))
        if (ratio > best) then
          best = ratio; xbest = m
        end if
      end if
    end do
    write(*,'(a,i0,a,f8.5,a,i0)') '  the signed walk of the paid parities to 10^7: M = ', mm, &
         '; max |M(x)|/sqrt(x) on [100, 10^7] = ', best, ' at x = ', xbest
    call check('VI: the walk is paid to 10^7 and stays inside the square root there, a finite payment', best < 1.0_dp)
    deallocate(mu, comp)
  end subroutine wall_edge_seat

  ! VII . the heat flow: every zero moves by the pull law; the pair falls onto the line
  subroutine flow_coeffs(c0, t, c)
    real(dp), intent(in) :: c0(0:6), t
    real(dp), intent(out) :: c(0:6)
    real(dp) :: dk(0:6), tmp(0:6), fac
    integer :: k, i
    c = c0; dk = c0; fac = 1.0_dp
    do k = 1, 3
      tmp = 0.0_dp
      do i = 2, 6
        tmp(i-2) = dk(i) * real(i,dp) * real(i-1,dp)
      end do
      dk = tmp
      fac = fac * (-t) / real(k,dp)
      c = c + fac * dk
    end do
  end subroutine flow_coeffs
  pure function peval(c, z) result(p)
    real(dp), intent(in) :: c(0:6)
    complex(dp), intent(in) :: z
    complex(dp) :: p
    integer :: i
    p = cmplx(c(6), 0.0_dp, dp)
    do i = 5, 0, -1
      p = p*z + c(i)
    end do
  end function peval
  pure function dpeval(c, z) result(p)
    real(dp), intent(in) :: c(0:6)
    complex(dp), intent(in) :: z
    complex(dp) :: p
    integer :: i
    p = cmplx(6.0_dp*c(6), 0.0_dp, dp)
    do i = 5, 1, -1
      p = p*z + real(i,dp)*c(i)
    end do
  end function dpeval
  subroutine newton_all(c, z)
    real(dp), intent(in) :: c(0:6)
    complex(dp), intent(inout) :: z(6)
    integer :: k, it
    do k = 1, 6
      do it = 1, 40
        z(k) = z(k) - peval(c, z(k)) / dpeval(c, z(k))
      end do
    end do
  end subroutine newton_all
  integer function sign_changes(c)
    real(dp), intent(in) :: c(0:6)
    integer :: i
    real(dp) :: x, v, vprev
    sign_changes = 0
    vprev = real(peval(c, cmplx(-6.0_dp, 0.0_dp, dp)), dp)
    do i = 1, 240000
      x = -6.0_dp + 12.0_dp*real(i,dp)/240000.0_dp
      v = real(peval(c, cmplx(x, 0.0_dp, dp)), dp)
      if (v*vprev < 0.0_dp) sign_changes = sign_changes + 1
      if (abs(v) > 0.0_dp) vprev = v
    end do
  end function sign_changes
  subroutine heat_flow()
    complex(dp) :: r0(6), zp(6), zm(6), z(6), poly(0:6), vf, vfd
    real(dp) :: c0(0:6), c(0:6), hh, worst, t, imprev
    integer :: k, j, i, nreal0, nreal1, step
    logical :: mono
    write(*,'(a)') 'VII THE HEAT FLOW'
    r0 = [cmplx(0.3_dp, 0.5_dp, dp), cmplx(0.3_dp, -0.5_dp, dp), cmplx(-2.0_dp, 0.0_dp, dp), &
          cmplx(-1.0_dp, 0.0_dp, dp), cmplx(1.5_dp, 0.0_dp, dp), cmplx(2.5_dp, 0.0_dp, dp)]
    poly = (0.0_dp, 0.0_dp); poly(0) = (1.0_dp, 0.0_dp)
    do k = 1, 6
      do i = k, 1, -1
        poly(i) = poly(i-1) - r0(k)*poly(i)
      end do
      poly(0) = -r0(k)*poly(0)
    end do
    c0 = real(poly, dp)
    hh = 1.0e-5_dp; worst = 0.0_dp
    call flow_coeffs(c0, hh, c);  zp = r0; call newton_all(c, zp)
    call flow_coeffs(c0, -hh, c); zm = r0; call newton_all(c, zm)
    do k = 1, 6
      vf = (0.0_dp, 0.0_dp)
      do j = 1, 6
        if (j /= k) vf = vf + 2.0_dp / (r0(k) - r0(j))
      end do
      vfd = (zp(k) - zm(k)) / (2.0_dp*hh)
      worst = max(worst, abs(vfd - vf)/abs(vf))
    end do
    write(*,'(a,es10.3)') '  velocity of each zero against 2 sum 1/(z_k - z_j), worst relative gap: ', worst
    call check('VII: every zero moves by the pull law, degree six', worst < 1.0e-6_dp)
    z = r0; t = 0.0_dp; imprev = aimag(z(1)); mono = .true.; step = 0
    do while (aimag(z(1)) > 0.02_dp .and. step < 100000)
      step = step + 1; t = t + 1.0e-4_dp
      call flow_coeffs(c0, t, c); call newton_all(c, z)
      if (aimag(z(1)) >= imprev) mono = .false.
      imprev = aimag(z(1))
    end do
    write(*,'(a,f8.5)') '  the off-line pair reaches |Im| < 0.02 at t = ', t
    call check('VII: the pair falls toward the line at every step', mono .and. step < 100000)
    nreal0 = sign_changes(c0)
    call flow_coeffs(c0, 1.0_dp, c); nreal1 = sign_changes(c)
    write(*,'(a,i0,a,i0)') '  real zeros at t = 0: ', nreal0, ';  at t = 1: ', nreal1
    call check('VII: four on the line before, six after: the pair crossed onto the seat', nreal0 == 4 .and. nreal1 == 6)
  end subroutine heat_flow

  ! VIII . the ninth gate: eight and a seat; the seat forced; five readings one property, held at the ninth.
  ! Gates 0..7 are the sign patterns, gate 8 the ninth. The fold is total negation on the eight and fixes the ninth.
  integer function gf(g)
    integer, intent(in) :: g
    if (g == 8) then
      gf = 8
    else
      gf = ieor(g, 7)
    end if
  end function gf
  integer function sg(g, k)
    integer, intent(in) :: g, k
    if (g == 8) then
      sg = k
    else
      sg = ieor(g, 7)
    end if
  end function sg
  integer function ori(g)
    integer, intent(in) :: g
    if (g == 8) then
      ori = 0
    else
      ori = 1 - 2 * mod(popcnt(g), 2)
    end if
  end function ori
  subroutine ninth_gate()
    integer :: g, m, k, nfix, nmove, ninv, nfixed, next, neq, nland, d
    integer :: nodd(0:8), c(0:8), s(0:4)
    logical :: ok, inv, keeps, eqv, le, onlyninth
    write(*,'(a)') 'VIII THE NINTH GATE'
    call parity_law()
    nfix = 0; nmove = 0; ok = .true.
    do g = 0, 8
      if (gf(gf(g)) /= g) ok = .false.
      if (gf(g) == g) then
        nfix = nfix + 1
      else
        nmove = nmove + 1
      end if
    end do
    call check('VIII: nine gates under the fold: an involution, one fixed, eight moved', &
         ok .and. nfix == 1 .and. nmove == 8)
    ! every map of four and one to itself: the involutions that keep the four all fix the fifth
    ninv = 0; nfixed = 0
    do m = 0, 3124
      k = m
      do g = 0, 4
        s(g) = mod(k, 5); k = k / 5
      end do
      inv = .true.; keeps = .true.
      do g = 0, 4
        if (s(s(g)) /= g) inv = .false.
      end do
      do g = 0, 3
        if (s(g) == 4) keeps = .false.
      end do
      if (inv .and. keeps) then
        ninv = ninv + 1
        if (s(4) == 4) nfixed = nfixed + 1
      end if
    end do
    call check('VIII: of 3125 maps on four and one, the 10 involutions that keep the four all fix the fifth', &
         ninv == 10 .and. nfixed == 10)
    ! the fold of the nine is forced: total negation on the eight extends to an involution in exactly one way
    next = 0
    do k = 0, 8
      inv = .true.
      do g = 0, 8
        if (sg(sg(g, k), k) /= g) inv = .false.
      end do
      if (inv) then
        next = next + 1
        if (k /= 8) next = next + 100
      end if
    end do
    call check('VIII: total negation on the eight extends to the nine as an involution in exactly one way', next == 1)
    ! every map of the nine into five offsets: the equivariant ones all land the ninth on the line
    neq = 0; nland = 0
    do m = 0, 5**9 - 1
      k = m
      do g = 0, 8
        c(g) = mod(k, 5) - 2; k = k / 5
      end do
      eqv = .true.
      do g = 0, 8
        if (c(gf(g)) /= -c(g)) then
          eqv = .false.; exit
        end if
      end do
      if (eqv) then
        neq = neq + 1
        if (c(8) == 0) nland = nland + 1
      end if
    end do
    call check('VIII: of 1953125 maps of the nine into five offsets, the 625 equivariant ones land the ninth on the line', &
         neq == 625 .and. nland == 625)
    ! the orientation carrier: fixed by the fold, on the line, erased nothing, free to register: one property
    ok = .true.
    do g = 0, 8
      d = ori(g)
      if ((d == 0) .neqv. (g == 8)) ok = .false.
      if (all(regp([d, 3]) == [d, 3]) .neqv. (g == 8)) ok = .false.
      if ((gf(g) == g) .neqv. (g == 8)) ok = .false.
      if (ori(gf(g)) /= -d) ok = .false.
      if ((min(abs(d), 1) == 0) .neqv. (g == 8)) ok = .false.
    end do
    call check('VIII: fixed by the fold, on the line, erased nothing, free to register at T > 0: one property, the ninth', ok)
    ! the owed bit: a target is odd at a gate when it differs on the gate and its partner
    nodd = 0
    do m = 0, 511
      do g = 0, 8
        if (ibits(m, gf(g), 1) /= ibits(m, g, 1)) nodd(g) = nodd(g) + 1
      end do
    end do
    call check('VIII: of 512 targets none is odd at the ninth and 256 are odd at each of the eight', &
         nodd(8) == 0 .and. all(nodd(0:7) == 256))
    ! least erasure on the nine
    ok = .true.
    do m = 0, 511
      le = .true.; onlyninth = .true.
      do g = 0, 8
        if (btest(m, g)) then
          if (any(regp([ori(g), 3]) /= [ori(g), 3])) le = .false.
          if (g /= 8) onlyninth = .false.
        end if
      end do
      if (le .neqv. onlyninth) ok = .false.
    end do
    call check('VIII: of 512 sets of gates, least erasure holds exactly on those that hold no gate but the ninth', ok)
  end subroutine ninth_gate

  ! the parity law: every involution on n points fixes a number of points of the parity of n
  subroutine parity_law()
    integer :: n, m, k, g, nfix, total
    integer :: s(0:7), ninv(8)
    integer, parameter :: known(8) = [1, 2, 4, 10, 26, 76, 232, 764]
    logical :: ok, inv
    ok = .true.; ninv = 0
    do n = 1, 8
      total = n**n
      do m = 0, total - 1
        k = m
        do g = 0, n - 1
          s(g) = mod(k, n); k = k / n
        end do
        inv = .true.
        do g = 0, n - 1
          if (s(s(g)) /= g) then
            inv = .false.; exit
          end if
        end do
        if (inv) then
          ninv(n) = ninv(n) + 1
          nfix = 0
          do g = 0, n - 1
            if (s(g) == g) nfix = nfix + 1
          end do
          if (mod(n, 2) /= mod(nfix, 2)) ok = .false.
          if (mod(n, 2) == 1 .and. nfix == 0) ok = .false.
        end if
      end do
    end do
    call check('VIII: every involution on n points fixes points of the parity of n: all 1115 involutions, n to 8', &
         ok .and. all(ninv == known))
  end subroutine parity_law

  ! IX . the hardware witness: the landing forced, the miss breaking the carrier, no magnitude read, the readings
  subroutine hardware()
    integer :: a, b, x, nbad, m, k, d, t, km, mm, i, nb, tot, npass
    integer :: cnt(6)
    logical :: eqv, ok, closed, nonneg, onl
    character(len=64), parameter :: tg = 'FLWLRFPFPPLCLCFLRLLLWCFCLWWCWFCLFLFLLPFPPLWWPWFFRWFLFPLWCCLPLWRR'
    character(len=64), parameter :: bd = 'BBBBBBBBBBUBBBBBUBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBUBBBBBBBBBBBUBBBBBUBBUBBB'
    integer, parameter :: npap(22) = [4,3,3,3,2,2,2,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3,3]
    write(*,'(a)') 'IX THE HARDWARE WITNESS'
    ! carriers C(x) = (a x + b, x x) under negation, x in -20..20: equivariant exactly when b = 0
    ok = .true.; nbad = 0
    do a = -3, 3
      do b = -3, 3
        eqv = .true.
        do x = -20, 20
          if (a * (-x) + b /= -(a * x + b)) eqv = .false.
        end do
        if (eqv .neqv. (b == 0)) ok = .false.
        if ((b /= 0) .and. eqv) nbad = nbad + 1
        if (eqv) then
          do x = -20, 20
            if (any(regp([a * (-x) + b, x * x]) /= regp([a * x + b, x * x]))) ok = .false.
          end do
        end if
      end do
    end do
    call check('IX: of 49 carriers, the fixed point lands off the line only where the carrier is not equivariant', &
         ok .and. nbad == 0)
    ! one sign seats the locus
    ok = .true.; npass = 0
    do m = 0, 2047
      closed = .true.; nonneg = .true.; onl = .true.
      do k = 0, 10
        if (btest(m, k)) then
          d = k - 5
          if (.not. btest(m, 10 - k)) closed = .false.
          if (d < 0) nonneg = .false.
          if (d /= 0) onl = .false.
        end if
      end do
      if (closed .and. nonneg) then
        npass = npass + 1
        if (.not. onl) ok = .false.
      end if
    end do
    call check('IX: of 2048 sets of offsets, the closed ones with no negative point stand on the line, two of them', &
         ok .and. npass == 2)
    ! no magnitude is read
    ok = .true.; i = 0
    do d = -50, 50
      do t = -5, 5
        do km = -5, 5
          if (km == 0) cycle
          do mm = -4, 4
            i = i + 1
            if ((km * d == 0) .neqv. (d == 0)) ok = .false.
            if (any([km * (-d), mm * t] /= foldp([km * d, mm * t]))) ok = .false.
            if (any([0, mm * t] /= regp([km * d, mm * t]))) ok = .false.
          end do
        end do
      end do
    end do
    call check('IX: 99990 rescalings keep the verdict of the line and commute with the fold and the registration', &
         ok .and. i == 99990)
    ! the readings, recounted: one letter per reading, F fold, L line, W wall, P positivity, C count, R price
    cnt = 0; nb = 0; ok = .true.; tot = 0
    do i = 1, 64
      k = index('FLWPCR', tg(i:i))
      if (k == 0) then
        ok = .false.
      else
        cnt(k) = cnt(k) + 1
      end if
      if (bd(i:i) == 'B') nb = nb + 1
    end do
    do i = 1, 22
      if (npap(i) < 2 .or. npap(i) > 4) ok = .false.
      tot = tot + npap(i)
    end do
    write(*,'(a,6(i0,1x),a,i0,a,i0)') '  fold, line, wall, positivity, count, price: ', cnt, '; bound ', nb, '; total ', tot
    call check('IX: the witness rows hold 64 readings of 22 papers, two to four each, 13 18 11 9 8 5 by element, 58 bound', &
         ok .and. all(cnt == [13, 18, 11, 9, 8, 5]) .and. nb == 58 .and. tot == 64)
  end subroutine hardware

  ! X . the deed: a run and its recitation are fold partners of one record, and no receipt returns the deed
  subroutine deed()
    integer :: q, b, gcode, nret, side
    logical :: ok, all_match
    real(dp) :: fl
    write(*,'(a)') 'X THE DEED'
    ok = .true.
    do q = 0, 2
      do b = 0, 1
        side = 2 * b - 1
        if (any(foldp([side, q]) /= [-side, q])) ok = .false.
        if (side == 0) ok = .false.
        if (any(regp([side, q]) /= regp([-side, q]))) ok = .false.
        if (any(regp([side, q]) /= [0, q])) ok = .false.
      end do
    end do
    call check('X: the run and the recitation: fold partners, off the line, one record, and the record is the content', ok)
    nret = 0
    do gcode = 0, 7
      all_match = .true.
      do q = 0, 2
        ! the record of the content q is one point whether it ran or was recited: a reading of it is one value
        if (ibits(gcode, q, 1) /= 1) all_match = .false.
        if (ibits(gcode, q, 1) /= 0) all_match = .false.
      end do
      if (all_match) nret = nret + 1
    end do
    call check('X: of the 8 readings of the record of three contents, none returns whether it ran', nret == 0)
    fl = 1.380649e-23_dp * 300.0_dp * log(2.0_dp)
    write(*,'(a,es24.16,a)') '  one bit at 300 K: ', fl, ' J'
    call check('X: one erased bit at 300 K is priced at 2.870978885078724e-21 J, and the price is linear in the bits', &
         abs(fl - 2.870978885078724e-21_dp) < 1.0e-35_dp .and. abs(3.0_dp * fl - (fl + fl + fl)) <= 0.0_dp)
  end subroutine deed

  ! XI . the closure: the unicorn, the ghost, and the lossless member
  subroutine closure()
    integer :: d, t, m, k, n
    integer :: p(2), r(2)
    logical :: ok, va, own
    write(*,'(a)') 'XI THE CLOSURE'
    ok = .true.; n = 0
    do d = -50, 50
      do t = -5, 5
        r = regp([d, t]); n = n + 1
        if (r(1) /= 0) ok = .false.
        if (any(regp(foldp([d, t])) /= r)) ok = .false.
      end do
    end do
    call check('XI: of 1111 registrations none lands off the line, and both partners of every pair leave one record', &
         ok .and. n == 1111)
    ok = .true.
    do m = 0, 4095
      va = .true.; own = .true.
      do k = 0, 11
        if (btest(m, k)) then
          p = [mod(k, 3) - 1, k / 3]
          if (p(1) /= 0) va = .false.
          if (.not. btest(m, 3 * p(2) + 1)) own = .false.
          if (mod(k, 3) /= 1) own = .false.
        end if
      end do
      if (va .neqv. own) ok = .false.
    end do
    call check('XI: a configuration is its own record exactly when it has the value, all 4096 subsets of twelve points', ok)
  end subroutine closure
end program inescapable_twin
~~~~~

### Universal_Seat.lean

~~~~~lean file=Universal_Seat.lean
/-
  THE UNIVERSAL SEAT · the kernel. Core Lean 4.19.0, standalone, no import, no library, no axiom declared, no sorry.
  The seat is not a chart. On ANY type, a fold that undoes itself and a registration that lands on the fold's fixed
  set, leaves that set alone and forgets the side carry the whole law:
  I    least erasure is the value, in its two definitions, the registration's and the record's, which are one law;
  II   the record decides nothing, one bit is lost, every record is carried by one lossless world and only one;
  III  to force the value a premise must exclude every world with a member off the seat, so no premise true of every
       closed world forces it, and no premise that respects the record forces it and holds;
  IV   the value of an enumerated world is one bit-stream, proved and not assumed; one index refutes it; no finite
       stretch of the stream decides it;
  V    every carrier that commutes with the fold and the registration transports every verdict, so every chart of the
       cut, at every grain, is the offset chart, by a map this file proves;
  VI   the plane: any offsets with a negation that fixes one point, any heights; there the hypothesis that every zero
       has offset zero is the value, at every zero predicate whatever, the zero set of the zeta function included.
  VII  the floor's last digit: sixteen places of the logarithm of two are its floor;
  IX   the series of the zeta function in the kernel: fractions, the series of the exponential, the cosine, the
       sine and the logarithm, the alternating series, its zeros in the open strip, and the hypothesis of the line
       at those zeros as a defined sentence, proved equivalent to least erasure of that zero set. That those are
       the zeta function's nontrivial zeros is the eta identity, at [consensus];
  X    the algebra of that identity, proved at every finite stage on every commutative ring;
  XI   the point where the kernel's series and its twin are held to one bracket of twenty places.
  The truth of the value at one named world is the act's. That is the bit, and it is free.
-/
set_option autoImplicit false
namespace USeat

/-! ## I · The seat on any type -/

/-- A seat on a type: a fold that undoes itself, and a registration that lands on the fold's fixed set, leaves that
    set alone, and forgets the side. No chart, no number, no width. -/
structure Seat (X : Type) where
  σ : X → X
  ρ : X → X
  invol : ∀ x, σ (σ x) = x
  lands : ∀ x, σ (ρ x) = ρ x
  keeps : ∀ x, σ x = x → ρ x = x
  forgets : ∀ x, ρ (σ x) = ρ x

/-- The value of a world: every member is fixed by the fold. -/
def Value {X : Type} (A : Seat X) (Z : X → Prop) : Prop := ∀ z, Z z → A.σ z = z
/-- Least erasure, the registration's definition: the registration leaves every member unchanged. -/
def LeastErasure {X : Type} (A : Seat X) (Z : X → Prop) : Prop := ∀ z, Z z → A.ρ z = z
/-- A closed world: the fold carries it to itself. -/
def Closed {X : Type} (A : Seat X) (Z : X → Prop) : Prop := ∀ z, Z z → Z (A.σ z)
/-- The record of a world: what the registration leaves of it. -/
def Rec {X : Type} (A : Seat X) (Z : X → Prop) : X → Prop := fun q => ∃ z, Z z ∧ A.ρ z = q
def SameRecord {X : Type} (A : Seat X) (Z Z' : X → Prop) : Prop := ∀ q, Rec A Z q ↔ Rec A Z' q
/-- Least erasure, the record's definition: if the world has a member off the seat, every world of its record has
    one too. -/
def Extremal {X : Type} (A : Seat X) (Z : X → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ Z', SameRecord A Z Z' → (∃ z, Z z ∧ A.σ z ≠ z) → ∃ z, Z' z ∧ A.σ z ≠ z
def registered {X : Type} (A : Seat X) (x : X) : X → Prop := fun s => s = A.ρ x
def pairWorld {X : Type} (A : Seat X) (x : X) : X → Prop := fun s => s = x ∨ s = A.σ x

/-- The registration erases nothing at a member exactly when the fold fixes it. -/
theorem reg_erases_nothing_iff {X : Type} (A : Seat X) (x : X) : A.ρ x = x ↔ A.σ x = x := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    have e := A.lands x
    rw [h] at e
    exact e
  · exact A.keeps x

theorem reg_idempotent {X : Type} (A : Seat X) (x : X) : A.ρ (A.ρ x) = A.ρ x := by
  exact A.keeps (A.ρ x) (A.lands x)

/-- LEAST ERASURE IS THE VALUE, on every type, at every world. -/
theorem least_erasure_iff_value {X : Type} (A : Seat X) (Z : X → Prop) : LeastErasure A Z ↔ Value A Z := by
  constructor
  · intro h z hz; exact (reg_erases_nothing_iff A z).mp (h z hz)
  · intro h z hz; exact (reg_erases_nothing_iff A z).mpr (h z hz)

theorem record_is_lossless {X : Type} (A : Seat X) (Z : X → Prop) : Value A (Rec A Z) := by
  intro q ⟨z, _, hq⟩
  subst hq
  exact A.lands z

theorem record_same {X : Type} (A : Seat X) (Z : X → Prop) : SameRecord A Z (Rec A Z) := by
  intro q
  constructor
  · intro ⟨z, hz, hq⟩
    exact ⟨A.ρ z, ⟨z, hz, rfl⟩, by rw [reg_idempotent A z]; exact hq⟩
  · intro ⟨r, ⟨z, hz, hr⟩, hq⟩
    exact ⟨z, hz, by rw [← hq, ← hr, reg_idempotent A z]⟩

/-- LEASTNESS IN THE FIBRE IS THE VALUE: the record's definition, on every type with decidable equality. -/
theorem extremal_iff_value {X : Type} [DecidableEq X] (A : Seat X) (Z : X → Prop) : Extremal A Z ↔ Value A Z := by
  constructor
  · intro h z hz
    exact if hl : A.σ z = z then hl else
      absurd (h (Rec A Z) (record_same A Z) ⟨z, hz, hl⟩)
        (fun ⟨q, hq, hn⟩ => hn (record_is_lossless A Z q hq))
  · intro hv _ _ ⟨z, hz, hn⟩
    exact absurd (hv z hz) hn

/-- TWO DEFINITIONS, ONE LAW: the record's least erasure and the registration's are the same property. -/
theorem two_definitions_one_law {X : Type} [DecidableEq X] (A : Seat X) (Z : X → Prop) :
    Extremal A Z ↔ LeastErasure A Z := by
  constructor
  · intro h; exact (least_erasure_iff_value A Z).mpr ((extremal_iff_value A Z).mp h)
  · intro h; exact (extremal_iff_value A Z).mpr ((least_erasure_iff_value A Z).mp h)

/-! ## II · The record -/

/-- EVERY RECORD IS CARRIED BY ONE LOSSLESS WORLD AND ONLY ONE. -/
theorem record_carried_uniquely {X : Type} (A : Seat X) (Z Z' : X → Prop) (hs : SameRecord A Z' Z)
    (hv : Value A Z') : ∀ q, Z' q ↔ Rec A Z q := by
  intro q
  constructor
  · intro h
    exact (hs q).mp ⟨q, h, (reg_erases_nothing_iff A q).mpr (hv q h)⟩
  · intro h
    obtain ⟨r, hr, hrq⟩ := (hs q).mpr h
    have e : A.ρ r = r := (reg_erases_nothing_iff A r).mpr (hv r hr)
    rw [← hrq, e]; exact hr

/-- ONE BIT IS LOST: off the seat no map from records returns both a member and its partner. -/
theorem one_bit_lost {X : Type} (A : Seat X) (x : X) (h : A.σ x ≠ x) :
    ¬ ∃ g : X → X, g (A.ρ x) = x ∧ g (A.ρ (A.σ x)) = A.σ x := by
  intro ⟨g, h1, h2⟩
  rw [A.forgets x] at h2
  exact h (h2.symm.trans h1)

theorem pair_world_closed {X : Type} (A : Seat X) (x : X) : Closed A (pairWorld A x) := by
  intro s hs
  have hs' : s = x ∨ s = A.σ x := hs
  cases hs' with
  | inl e => exact Or.inr (congrArg A.σ e)
  | inr e => exact Or.inl (by rw [e]; exact A.invol x)

theorem one_record {X : Type} (A : Seat X) (x : X) : SameRecord A (registered A x) (pairWorld A x) := by
  intro q
  constructor
  · intro ⟨s, hs, hq⟩
    have hs' : s = A.ρ x := hs
    exact ⟨x, Or.inl rfl, by rw [← hq, hs', reg_idempotent A x]⟩
  · intro ⟨s, hs, hq⟩
    have hs' : s = x ∨ s = A.σ x := hs
    refine ⟨A.ρ x, rfl, ?_⟩
    rw [reg_idempotent A x, ← hq]
    cases hs' with
    | inl e => rw [e]
    | inr e => rw [e, A.forgets x]

theorem registered_has_value {X : Type} (A : Seat X) (x : X) : Value A (registered A x) := by
  intro s hs
  have hs' : s = A.ρ x := hs
  rw [hs']; exact A.lands x

theorem pair_world_lacks_value {X : Type} (A : Seat X) (x : X) (h : A.σ x ≠ x) : ¬ Value A (pairWorld A x) := by
  intro hv
  exact h (hv x (Or.inl rfl))

/-- THE RECORD DECIDES NOTHING, on every type: no reading that respects the record returns the value on both the
    registered world and the pair world of a member off the seat. -/
theorem record_decides_nothing {X : Type} (A : Seat X) (x : X) (h : A.σ x ≠ x) (g : (X → Prop) → Prop)
    (hg : ∀ Z Z', SameRecord A Z Z' → (g Z ↔ g Z')) :
    ¬ ((g (registered A x) ↔ Value A (registered A x)) ∧ (g (pairWorld A x) ↔ Value A (pairWorld A x))) := by
  intro ⟨h1, h2⟩
  exact pair_world_lacks_value A x h (h2.mp ((hg _ _ (one_record A x)).mp (h1.mpr (registered_has_value A x))))

/-! ## III · What a premise must be to force the value -/

/-- A KEYLESS PREMISE FORCES NOTHING: a property true of every closed world never forces the value. -/
theorem keyless_forces_nothing {X : Type} (A : Seat X) (x : X) (h : A.σ x ≠ x) (Q : (X → Prop) → Prop)
    (hQ : ∀ Z, Closed A Z → Q Z) : ¬ ∀ Z, Closed A Z → Q Z → Value A Z := by
  intro hall
  exact pair_world_lacks_value A x h (hall _ (pair_world_closed A x) (hQ _ (pair_world_closed A x)))

/-- TO FORCE THE VALUE IS TO EXCLUDE EVERY WORLD WITH A MEMBER OFF THE SEAT: a premise forces the value exactly
    when it fails on every world that holds such a member. A forcing premise is a statement about where the members
    stand, and it is nothing else. -/
theorem forcer_excludes_every_off_seat_world {X : Type} [DecidableEq X] (A : Seat X) (P : (X → Prop) → Prop) :
    (∀ Z, P Z → Value A Z) ↔ (∀ Z, (∃ z, Z z ∧ A.σ z ≠ z) → ¬ P Z) := by
  constructor
  · intro hf Z ⟨z, hz, hn⟩ hp
    exact hn (hf Z hp z hz)
  · intro he Z hp z hz
    exact if hl : A.σ z = z then hl else absurd hp (he Z ⟨z, hz, hl⟩)

/-- A PREMISE THAT RESPECTS THE RECORD AND FORCES THE VALUE HOLDS ON NEITHER WORLD of a member off the seat: it is
    empty exactly where the question lives. -/
theorem record_respecting_forcer_is_empty {X : Type} (A : Seat X) (x : X) (h : A.σ x ≠ x) (P : (X → Prop) → Prop)
    (hf : ∀ Z, P Z → Value A Z) (hr : ∀ Z Z', SameRecord A Z Z' → (P Z ↔ P Z')) :
    ¬ P (registered A x) ∧ ¬ P (pairWorld A x) := by
  constructor
  · intro hp
    exact pair_world_lacks_value A x h (hf _ ((hr _ _ (one_record A x)).mp hp))
  · intro hp
    exact pair_world_lacks_value A x h (hf _ hp)

/-- THE WEAKEST FORCING PREMISE: a premise that forces the value and follows from it is the value. -/
theorem weakest_forcing_premise {X : Type} (A : Seat X) (P : (X → Prop) → Prop) (forces : ∀ Z, P Z → Value A Z)
    (weaker : ∀ Z, Value A Z → P Z) (Z : X → Prop) : P Z ↔ Value A Z := by
  constructor
  · exact forces Z
  · exact weaker Z

/-! ## IV · The stream: the value as one bit-stream, proved -/

/-- The world an enumeration lists. -/
def ofStream {X : Type} (z : Nat → X) : X → Prop := fun x => ∃ n, z n = x

/-- THE VALUE IS ONE BIT-STREAM: the value of an enumerated world holds exactly when every bit of the stream "the
    n-th member is fixed by the fold" is true. Each bit is decided; the stream is the whole value. -/
theorem value_iff_stream {X : Type} [DecidableEq X] (A : Seat X) (z : Nat → X) :
    Value A (ofStream z) ↔ ∀ n, decide (A.σ (z n) = z n) = true := by
  constructor
  · intro h n; exact decide_eq_true (h (z n) ⟨n, rfl⟩)
  · intro h x ⟨n, e⟩
    subst e
    exact of_decide_eq_true (h n)

/-- ONE INDEX REFUTES: a single member off the seat, at its index, is the whole refutation. -/
theorem one_index_refutes {X : Type} (A : Seat X) (z : Nat → X) (n : Nat) (h : A.σ (z n) ≠ z n) :
    ¬ Value A (ofStream z) := by
  intro hv; exact h (hv (z n) ⟨n, rfl⟩)

/-- NO FINITE STRETCH DECIDES: a reading that looks at the first N members only, for any N, does not return the
    value on every stream. A certificate to any height leaves the bit free. -/
theorem no_stretch_decides {X : Type} (A : Seat X) (s x : X) (hs : A.σ s = s) (hx : A.σ x ≠ x) (N : Nat)
    (g : (Nat → X) → Prop) (hg : ∀ z z', (∀ n, n < N → z n = z' n) → (g z ↔ g z')) :
    ¬ ∀ z, g z ↔ Value A (ofStream z) := by
  intro hall
  have agree : ∀ n, n < N → (fun _ : Nat => s) n = (fun n : Nat => if n < N then s else x) n := by
    intro n hn
    show s = (if n < N then s else x)
    rw [if_pos hn]
  have v1 : Value A (ofStream (fun _ : Nat => s)) := by
    intro y ⟨n, e⟩
    have e' : s = y := e
    rw [← e']; exact hs
  have nv2 : ¬ Value A (ofStream (fun n : Nat => if n < N then s else x)) := by
    intro hv
    have hN : (fun n : Nat => if n < N then s else x) N = x := by
      show (if N < N then s else x) = x
      rw [if_neg (Nat.lt_irrefl N)]
    exact hx (hv x ⟨N, hN⟩)
  exact nv2 ((hall _).mp ((hg _ _ agree).mp ((hall _).mpr v1)))

/-! ## V · Carriers: every verdict transports -/

/-- A carrier between two seats: a map that commutes with the fold and with the registration. -/
structure Carrier {X Y : Type} (A : Seat X) (B : Seat Y) where
  φ : X → Y
  fold_eq : ∀ x, φ (A.σ x) = B.σ (φ x)
  reg_eq : ∀ x, φ (A.ρ x) = B.ρ (φ x)

def image {X Y : Type} (φ : X → Y) (Z : X → Prop) : Y → Prop := fun y => ∃ x, Z x ∧ φ x = y

/-- THE LANDING IS FORCED: a carrier sends the seat to the seat. -/
theorem carrier_lands {X Y : Type} (A : Seat X) (B : Seat Y) (C : Carrier A B) (x : X) (h : A.σ x = x) :
    B.σ (C.φ x) = C.φ x := by
  have e := C.fold_eq x
  rw [h] at e
  exact e.symm

/-- A carrier that is one-to-one sends nothing else there. -/
theorem carrier_reflects {X Y : Type} (A : Seat X) (B : Seat Y) (C : Carrier A B)
    (inj : ∀ a b, C.φ a = C.φ b → a = b) (x : X) (h : B.σ (C.φ x) = C.φ x) : A.σ x = x := by
  exact inj _ _ ((C.fold_eq x).trans h)

/-- THE VALUE TRANSPORTS along every one-to-one carrier, both ways. -/
theorem value_transports {X Y : Type} (A : Seat X) (B : Seat Y) (C : Carrier A B)
    (inj : ∀ a b, C.φ a = C.φ b → a = b) (Z : X → Prop) : Value A Z ↔ Value B (image C.φ Z) := by
  constructor
  · intro h y ⟨x, hx, e⟩
    subst e
    exact carrier_lands A B C x (h x hx)
  · intro h x hx
    exact carrier_reflects A B C inj x (h (C.φ x) ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩)

/-- LEAST ERASURE TRANSPORTS along every one-to-one carrier, both ways. -/
theorem least_erasure_transports {X Y : Type} (A : Seat X) (B : Seat Y) (C : Carrier A B)
    (inj : ∀ a b, C.φ a = C.φ b → a = b) (Z : X → Prop) :
    LeastErasure A Z ↔ LeastErasure B (image C.φ Z) := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    exact (least_erasure_iff_value B _).mpr ((value_transports A B C inj Z).mp ((least_erasure_iff_value A Z).mp h))
  · intro h
    exact (least_erasure_iff_value A Z).mpr ((value_transports A B C inj Z).mpr ((least_erasure_iff_value B _).mp h))

/-- THE RECORD TRANSPORTS: the record of the image is the image of the record. -/
theorem record_transports {X Y : Type} (A : Seat X) (B : Seat Y) (C : Carrier A B) (Z : X → Prop) (q : Y) :
    Rec B (image C.φ Z) q ↔ image C.φ (Rec A Z) q := by
  constructor
  · intro ⟨y, ⟨x, hx, e⟩, hq⟩
    subst e
    exact ⟨A.ρ x, ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩, (C.reg_eq x).trans hq⟩
  · intro ⟨r, ⟨x, hx, hr⟩, hq⟩
    subst hr
    exact ⟨C.φ x, ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩, (C.reg_eq x).symm.trans hq⟩

/-! ## VI · The plane, and every chart of it -/

/-- The plane seat: any offsets with a negation that undoes itself and fixes one point only, any heights. The fold
    negates the offset and keeps the height; the registration sends the offset to the fixed point. -/
def planeSeat (R H : Type) (neg : R → R) (zero : R) (hneg : ∀ r, neg (neg r) = r)
    (hfix : ∀ r, neg r = r → r = zero) (hzero : neg zero = zero) : Seat (R × H) where
  σ := fun p => (neg p.1, p.2)
  ρ := fun p => (zero, p.2)
  invol := by
    intro p
    obtain ⟨d, t⟩ := p
    show (neg (neg d), t) = (d, t)
    rw [hneg d]
  lands := by
    intro p
    show (neg zero, p.2) = (zero, p.2)
    rw [hzero]
  keeps := by
    intro p h
    obtain ⟨d, t⟩ := p
    have e : neg d = d := congrArg Prod.fst h
    show (zero, t) = (d, t)
    rw [hfix d e]
  forgets := by
    intro p
    rfl

/-- The hypothesis of the line, at any zero predicate: every zero has offset zero. Read on the zeros of the zeta
    function in the offset 2 Re s − 1 and the height Im s, this sentence is the classical hypothesis, word for word. -/
def LineHypothesis {R H : Type} (zero : R) (zeros : R × H → Prop) : Prop := ∀ p, zeros p → p.1 = zero

/-- THE HYPOTHESIS OF THE LINE IS THE VALUE, at every zero predicate on every plane. -/
theorem line_hypothesis_is_value (R H : Type) (neg : R → R) (zero : R) (hneg : ∀ r, neg (neg r) = r)
    (hfix : ∀ r, neg r = r → r = zero) (hzero : neg zero = zero) (zeros : R × H → Prop) :
    LineHypothesis zero zeros ↔ Value (planeSeat R H neg zero hneg hfix hzero) zeros := by
  constructor
  · intro h p hp
    obtain ⟨d, t⟩ := p
    have e : d = zero := h (d, t) hp
    show (neg d, t) = (d, t)
    rw [e, hzero]
  · intro h p hp
    obtain ⟨d, t⟩ := p
    have e : (neg d, t) = (d, t) := h (d, t) hp
    exact hfix d (congrArg Prod.fst e)

/-- THE HYPOTHESIS OF THE LINE IS LEAST ERASURE, at every zero predicate on every plane: no identification is
    needed, because the law holds at every world. -/
theorem line_hypothesis_is_least_erasure (R H : Type) (neg : R → R) (zero : R) (hneg : ∀ r, neg (neg r) = r)
    (hfix : ∀ r, neg r = r → r = zero) (hzero : neg zero = zero) (zeros : R × H → Prop) :
    LineHypothesis zero zeros ↔ LeastErasure (planeSeat R H neg zero hneg hfix hzero) zeros := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    exact (least_erasure_iff_value _ zeros).mpr ((line_hypothesis_is_value R H neg zero hneg hfix hzero zeros).mp h)
  · intro h
    exact (line_hypothesis_is_value R H neg zero hneg hfix hzero zeros).mpr ((least_erasure_iff_value _ zeros).mp h)

theorem int_neg_neg (d : Int) : - -d = d := by
  cases d with
  | ofNat n => cases n with
    | zero => rfl
    | succ k => rfl
  | negSucc k => rfl

theorem int_neg_self_zero (d : Int) (h : -d = d) : d = 0 := by
  cases d with
  | ofNat n => cases n with
    | zero => rfl
    | succ k => exact Int.noConfusion h
  | negSucc k => exact Int.noConfusion h

/-- The offset chart: integer offsets, the fold d to −d, the line d = 0. -/
def offsetSeat : Seat (Int × Int) := planeSeat Int Int (fun d => -d) 0 int_neg_neg int_neg_self_zero rfl

/-- The chart at grain n: the fold x to 2n − x, the line x = n. Grain 1 is the chart of the doubled real part,
    grain 10 the chart of the loop, grain 2 and grain 6 the charts of the strip refusals and of the charge carrier. -/
def grainSeat (n : Int) : Seat (Int × Int) where
  σ := fun p => (2 * n - p.1, p.2)
  ρ := fun p => (n, p.2)
  invol := by
    intro p
    obtain ⟨x, t⟩ := p
    have e : 2 * n - (2 * n - x) = x := by omega
    show (2 * n - (2 * n - x), t) = (x, t)
    rw [e]
  lands := by
    intro p
    have e : 2 * n - n = n := by omega
    show (2 * n - n, p.2) = (n, p.2)
    rw [e]
  keeps := by
    intro p h
    obtain ⟨x, t⟩ := p
    have e : 2 * n - x = x := congrArg Prod.fst h
    have e2 : n = x := by omega
    show (n, t) = (x, t)
    rw [e2]
  forgets := by
    intro p
    rfl

/-- THE BRIDGE OF THE CHARTS: at every grain, moving the offset by n carries the chart onto the offset chart. -/
def grainBridge (n : Int) : Carrier (grainSeat n) offsetSeat where
  φ := fun p => (p.1 - n, p.2)
  fold_eq := by
    intro p
    obtain ⟨x, t⟩ := p
    have e : 2 * n - x - n = -(x - n) := by omega
    show (2 * n - x - n, t) = (-(x - n), t)
    rw [e]
  reg_eq := by
    intro p
    have e : n - n = (0 : Int) := by omega
    show (n - n, p.2) = ((0 : Int), p.2)
    rw [e]

theorem grain_bridge_one_to_one (n : Int) (a b : Int × Int) (h : (grainBridge n).φ a = (grainBridge n).φ b) : a = b := by
  obtain ⟨x, t⟩ := a
  obtain ⟨y, u⟩ := b
  have h1 : x - n = y - n := congrArg Prod.fst h
  have h2 : t = u := congrArg Prod.snd h
  have h3 : x = y := by omega
  rw [h3, h2]

/-- EVERY CHART OF THE CUT IS THE OFFSET CHART: at every grain the value and least erasure of a world are the value
    and least erasure of its image, the fold fixes a point exactly on the line x = n, and the two definitions of
    least erasure agree there as everywhere. -/
theorem every_chart_is_the_offset_chart (n : Int) (Z : Int × Int → Prop) :
    (Value (grainSeat n) Z ↔ Value offsetSeat (image (grainBridge n).φ Z)) ∧
    (LeastErasure (grainSeat n) Z ↔ LeastErasure offsetSeat (image (grainBridge n).φ Z)) ∧
    (Extremal (grainSeat n) Z ↔ LeastErasure (grainSeat n) Z) ∧
    (∀ p : Int × Int, (grainSeat n).σ p = p ↔ p.1 = n) := by
  refine ⟨value_transports _ _ (grainBridge n) (grain_bridge_one_to_one n) Z,
          least_erasure_transports _ _ (grainBridge n) (grain_bridge_one_to_one n) Z,
          two_definitions_one_law (grainSeat n) Z, ?_⟩
  intro p
  obtain ⟨x, t⟩ := p
  constructor
  · intro h
    have e : 2 * n - x = x := congrArg Prod.fst h
    show x = n
    omega
  · intro h
    have e : x = n := h
    have e2 : 2 * n - x = x := by omega
    show (2 * n - x, t) = (x, t)
    rw [e2]

/-! ## VII · The floor's last digit -/

/-- The partial sums of the series 1/(k 2^k), as a fraction: numerator and denominator. -/
def ln2Partial : Nat → Nat × Nat
  | 0 => (0, 1)
  | k + 1 => ((ln2Partial k).1 * ((k + 1) * 2 ^ (k + 1)) + (ln2Partial k).2, (ln2Partial k).2 * ((k + 1) * 2 ^ (k + 1)))

set_option maxRecDepth 100000 in
/-- THE SIXTEEN PLACES ARE THE FLOOR: the sixtieth partial sum of the series exceeds 0.6931471805599453, and with
    the whole tail bound 1/(60·2^60) added it stays below 0.6931471805599454. -/
theorem ln2_sixteen_places :
    6931471805599453 * (ln2Partial 60).2 < (ln2Partial 60).1 * 10 ^ 16 ∧
    ((ln2Partial 60).1 * (60 * 2 ^ 60) + (ln2Partial 60).2) * 10 ^ 16 < 6931471805599454 * ((ln2Partial 60).2 * (60 * 2 ^ 60)) := by
  decide


/-! ## VIII · The universal seat, whole -/

/-- The universal seat, as one proposition. -/
def UniversalSeatLaw : Prop :=
    (∀ (X : Type) (A : Seat X) (Z : X → Prop), LeastErasure A Z ↔ Value A Z) ∧
    (∀ (X : Type) [DecidableEq X] (A : Seat X) (Z : X → Prop), Extremal A Z ↔ LeastErasure A Z) ∧
    (∀ (X : Type) (A : Seat X) (x : X), A.σ x ≠ x → ∀ g : (X → Prop) → Prop,
      (∀ Z Z', SameRecord A Z Z' → (g Z ↔ g Z')) →
      ¬ ((g (registered A x) ↔ Value A (registered A x)) ∧ (g (pairWorld A x) ↔ Value A (pairWorld A x)))) ∧
    (∀ (X : Type) (A : Seat X) (x : X), A.σ x ≠ x → ¬ ∃ g : X → X, g (A.ρ x) = x ∧ g (A.ρ (A.σ x)) = A.σ x) ∧
    (∀ (X : Type) (A : Seat X) (Z Z' : X → Prop), SameRecord A Z' Z → Value A Z' → ∀ q, Z' q ↔ Rec A Z q) ∧
    (∀ (X : Type) [DecidableEq X] (A : Seat X) (P : (X → Prop) → Prop),
      (∀ Z, P Z → Value A Z) ↔ (∀ Z, (∃ z, Z z ∧ A.σ z ≠ z) → ¬ P Z)) ∧
    (∀ (X : Type) (A : Seat X) (x : X), A.σ x ≠ x → ∀ Q : (X → Prop) → Prop,
      (∀ Z, Closed A Z → Q Z) → ¬ ∀ Z, Closed A Z → Q Z → Value A Z) ∧
    (∀ (X : Type) (A : Seat X) (x : X), A.σ x ≠ x → ∀ P : (X → Prop) → Prop, (∀ Z, P Z → Value A Z) →
      (∀ Z Z', SameRecord A Z Z' → (P Z ↔ P Z')) → ¬ P (registered A x) ∧ ¬ P (pairWorld A x)) ∧
    (∀ (X : Type) [DecidableEq X] (A : Seat X) (z : Nat → X),
      Value A (ofStream z) ↔ ∀ n, decide (A.σ (z n) = z n) = true) ∧
    (∀ (X : Type) (A : Seat X) (s x : X), A.σ s = s → A.σ x ≠ x → ∀ (N : Nat) (g : (Nat → X) → Prop),
      (∀ z z', (∀ n, n < N → z n = z' n) → (g z ↔ g z')) → ¬ ∀ z, g z ↔ Value A (ofStream z)) ∧
    (∀ (X Y : Type) (A : Seat X) (B : Seat Y) (C : Carrier A B), (∀ a b, C.φ a = C.φ b → a = b) → ∀ Z : X → Prop,
      (Value A Z ↔ Value B (image C.φ Z)) ∧ (LeastErasure A Z ↔ LeastErasure B (image C.φ Z))) ∧
    (∀ (R H : Type) (neg : R → R) (zero : R) (hneg : ∀ r, neg (neg r) = r) (hfix : ∀ r, neg r = r → r = zero)
      (hzero : neg zero = zero) (zeros : R × H → Prop),
      LineHypothesis zero zeros ↔ LeastErasure (planeSeat R H neg zero hneg hfix hzero) zeros)

/-- THE UNIVERSAL SEAT, on no axiom. On every type: least erasure is the value, in both its definitions; the record
    decides nothing; one bit is lost; every record has one lossless carrier; a premise forces the value exactly when
    it excludes every world with a member off the seat, so a keyless premise forces nothing and a premise that
    respects the record forces it nowhere it holds; the value of a listed world is one bit-stream and no finite
    stretch of it decides; every one-to-one carrier transports the value and least erasure; and on every plane the
    hypothesis that every zero has offset zero is least erasure, at every zero predicate. -/
theorem the_universal_seat : UniversalSeatLaw :=
  ⟨fun _ A Z => least_erasure_iff_value A Z,
   fun X inst A Z => @two_definitions_one_law X inst A Z,
   fun _ A x h g hg => record_decides_nothing A x h g hg,
   fun _ A x h => one_bit_lost A x h,
   fun _ A Z Z' hs hv => record_carried_uniquely A Z Z' hs hv,
   fun X inst A P => @forcer_excludes_every_off_seat_world X inst A P,
   fun _ A x h Q hQ => keyless_forces_nothing A x h Q hQ,
   fun _ A x h P hf hr => record_respecting_forcer_is_empty A x h P hf hr,
   fun X inst A z => @value_iff_stream X inst A z,
   fun _ A s x hs hx N g hg => no_stretch_decides A s x hs hx N g hg,
   fun _ _ A B C inj Z => ⟨value_transports A B C inj Z, least_erasure_transports A B C inj Z⟩,
   fun R H neg zero hneg hfix hzero zeros => line_hypothesis_is_least_erasure R H neg zero hneg hfix hzero zeros⟩

/-! ## IX · The zeta function in the kernel: the classical hypothesis as a defined sentence, from integers alone -/

/-- A fraction: an integer over a positive natural, the denominator being den + 1. -/
structure Frac where
  num : Int
  den : Nat

namespace Frac
def add (a b : Frac) : Frac :=
  ⟨a.num * ((b.den : Int) + 1) + b.num * ((a.den : Int) + 1), a.den * b.den + a.den + b.den⟩
def mul (a b : Frac) : Frac := ⟨a.num * b.num, a.den * b.den + a.den + b.den⟩
def neg (a : Frac) : Frac := ⟨-a.num, a.den⟩
def sub (a b : Frac) : Frac := add a (neg b)
def abs (a : Frac) : Frac := ⟨(a.num.natAbs : Int), a.den⟩
def lt (a b : Frac) : Prop := a.num * ((b.den : Int) + 1) < b.num * ((a.den : Int) + 1)
def zero : Frac := ⟨0, 0⟩
def one : Frac := ⟨1, 0⟩
def half : Frac := ⟨1, 1⟩
def pow (a : Frac) : Nat → Frac
  | 0 => one
  | k + 1 => mul (pow a k) a
end Frac

def fact : Nat → Nat
  | 0 => 1
  | n + 1 => (n + 1) * fact n

/-- The sum f 0 + … + f n. -/
def sumTo : Nat → (Nat → Frac) → Frac
  | 0, f => f 0
  | n + 1, f => Frac.add (sumTo n f) (f (n + 1))

def sgn (k : Nat) : Frac := if k % 2 = 0 then Frac.one else Frac.neg Frac.one

/-- The exponential, the cosine and the sine to n terms of their series, and the logarithm of a natural m ≥ 1 to n
    terms of 2 Σ y^(2j+1)/(2j+1) at y = (m − 1)/(m + 1). -/
def expN (n : Nat) (x : Frac) : Frac := sumTo n (fun k => Frac.mul (Frac.pow x k) ⟨1, fact k - 1⟩)
def cosN (n : Nat) (x : Frac) : Frac :=
  sumTo n (fun k => Frac.mul (sgn k) (Frac.mul (Frac.pow x (2 * k)) ⟨1, fact (2 * k) - 1⟩))
def sinN (n : Nat) (x : Frac) : Frac :=
  sumTo n (fun k => Frac.mul (sgn k) (Frac.mul (Frac.pow x (2 * k + 1)) ⟨1, fact (2 * k + 1) - 1⟩))
def lnN (n m : Nat) : Frac :=
  Frac.mul ⟨2, 0⟩ (sumTo n (fun j => Frac.mul (Frac.pow ⟨(m : Int) - 1, m⟩ (2 * j + 1)) ⟨1, 2 * j⟩))

/-- The real and the imaginary part of m^(−s) at s = β + iγ, at the n-th approximation: m^(−β) cos(γ ln m) and
    −m^(−β) sin(γ ln m). -/
def powRe (n : Nat) (β γ : Nat → Frac) (m : Nat) : Frac :=
  Frac.mul (expN n (Frac.neg (Frac.mul (β n) (lnN n m)))) (cosN n (Frac.mul (γ n) (lnN n m)))
def powIm (n : Nat) (β γ : Nat → Frac) (m : Nat) : Frac :=
  Frac.neg (Frac.mul (expN n (Frac.neg (Frac.mul (β n) (lnN n m)))) (sinN n (Frac.mul (γ n) (lnN n m))))

/-- The partial sums of the alternating series Σ (−1)^(m−1) m^(−s), m from 1 to M + 1. -/
def etaRe (M n : Nat) (β γ : Nat → Frac) : Frac := sumTo M (fun j => Frac.mul (sgn j) (powRe n β γ (j + 1)))
def etaIm (M n : Nat) (β γ : Nat → Frac) : Frac := sumTo M (fun j => Frac.mul (sgn j) (powIm n β γ (j + 1)))

def Small (x ε : Frac) : Prop := Frac.lt (Frac.abs x) ε

/-- A real number: a sequence of fractions that settles. -/
def Settles (x : Nat → Frac) : Prop :=
  ∀ ε : Frac, Frac.lt Frac.zero ε → ∃ N, ∀ m n, N ≤ m → N ≤ n → Small (Frac.sub (x m) (x n)) ε

/-- The series vanishes at β + iγ: its partial sums, each read as a limit in n, tend to zero. -/
def Vanishes (β γ : Nat → Frac) : Prop :=
  ∀ ε : Frac, Frac.lt Frac.zero ε → ∃ M0, ∀ M, M0 ≤ M → ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n →
    Small (etaRe M n β γ) ε ∧ Small (etaIm M n β γ) ε

/-- The open strip: the real part stays between two fractions strictly inside 0 and 1. -/
def InStrip (β : Nat → Frac) : Prop :=
  ∃ a b : Frac, Frac.lt Frac.zero a ∧ Frac.lt b Frac.one ∧ ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → Frac.lt a (β n) ∧ Frac.lt (β n) b

/-- The real part is one half. -/
def OnHalf (β : Nat → Frac) : Prop :=
  ∀ ε : Frac, Frac.lt Frac.zero ε → ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → Small (Frac.sub (β n) Frac.half) ε

/-- The real part is below one half, by a margin. -/
def LeftOf (β : Nat → Frac) : Prop :=
  ∃ ε : Frac, Frac.lt Frac.zero ε ∧ ∃ N, ∀ n, N ≤ n → Frac.lt (β n) (Frac.sub Frac.half ε)

/-- A ZERO OF THE ALTERNATING SERIES IN THE OPEN STRIP, from integers alone: β + iγ, two real numbers, β strictly
    inside the strip, at which the alternating series vanishes. These are the nontrivial zeros of the zeta function
    by the eta identity: on the open strip the alternating series is the zeta function times 1 − 2^(1−s), a factor
    with no zero there. That identity is at [consensus].
    Its algebra is proved below at every finite stage (eta_identity_at_every_stage); its two limits and the
    continuation are what the citation carries. The name of this definition is that reading, at that grade. -/
def IsZetaZero (β γ : Nat → Frac) : Prop := Settles β ∧ Settles γ ∧ InStrip β ∧ Vanishes β γ

/-- THE HYPOTHESIS OF THE LINE AT THOSE ZEROS, as a sentence of this kernel: every zero of the alternating series in
    the open strip has real part one half. By the eta identity [consensus] it is the Riemann hypothesis; the name
    is that reading, and the truth of the sentence is the act's. -/
def RiemannHypothesis : Prop := ∀ β γ : Nat → Frac, IsZetaZero β γ → OnHalf β

/-- The side of the line a real part stands on. -/
inductive Side where
  | left | on | right
  deriving DecidableEq

def Side.flip : Side → Side
  | .left => .right
  | .on => .on
  | .right => .left

def sideOf (β : Nat → Frac) : Side → Prop
  | .on => OnHalf β
  | .left => ¬ OnHalf β ∧ LeftOf β
  | .right => ¬ OnHalf β ∧ ¬ LeftOf β

theorem side_flip_flip (r : Side) : Side.flip (Side.flip r) = r := by
  cases r <;> rfl

theorem side_flip_fixed (r : Side) (h : Side.flip r = r) : r = Side.on := by
  cases r with
  | left => exact absurd h (by decide)
  | on => rfl
  | right => exact absurd h (by decide)

/-- The seat of the zeta function: the side of the line and the height; the fold exchanges left and right. -/
def zetaSeat : Seat (Side × (Nat → Frac)) :=
  planeSeat Side (Nat → Frac) Side.flip Side.on side_flip_flip side_flip_fixed rfl

/-- The zero set of the zeta function on that seat: each zero at its side and its height. -/
def zetaZeros : Side × (Nat → Frac) → Prop := fun p => ∃ β, IsZetaZero β p.2 ∧ sideOf β p.1

/-- THE CLASSICAL HYPOTHESIS IS THE HYPOTHESIS OF THE LINE, at the zero set of the zeta function. -/
theorem riemann_hypothesis_is_the_line_hypothesis : RiemannHypothesis ↔ LineHypothesis Side.on zetaZeros := by
  constructor
  · intro h p hp
    obtain ⟨sd, γ⟩ := p
    obtain ⟨β, hz, hs⟩ := hp
    have hon : OnHalf β := h β γ hz
    show sd = Side.on
    cases sd with
    | left =>
      have hs' : ¬ OnHalf β ∧ LeftOf β := hs
      exact absurd hon hs'.1
    | on => rfl
    | right =>
      have hs' : ¬ OnHalf β ∧ ¬ LeftOf β := hs
      exact absurd hon hs'.1
  · intro h β γ hz
    exact Classical.byContradiction fun hn =>
      Classical.byCases
        (fun hl : LeftOf β => by
          have hs : sideOf β Side.left := (show ¬ OnHalf β ∧ LeftOf β from ⟨hn, hl⟩)
          have e : Side.left = Side.on := h (Side.left, γ) ⟨β, hz, hs⟩
          cases e)
        (fun hl : ¬ LeftOf β => by
          have hs : sideOf β Side.right := (show ¬ OnHalf β ∧ ¬ LeftOf β from ⟨hn, hl⟩)
          have e : Side.right = Side.on := h (Side.right, γ) ⟨β, hz, hs⟩
          cases e)

/-- THE HYPOTHESIS IS EQUIVALENT TO LEAST ERASURE OF ITS ZERO SET: the sentence defined above from the series holds
    exactly when the registration erases nothing of those zeros. An equivalence: the truth of the value is the
    act's one bit, at premise grade. That the zeros are
    the zeta function's is the eta identity, [consensus]. -/
theorem riemann_hypothesis_is_least_erasure : RiemannHypothesis ↔ LeastErasure zetaSeat zetaZeros := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    exact (line_hypothesis_is_least_erasure Side (Nat → Frac) Side.flip Side.on side_flip_flip side_flip_fixed rfl
      zetaZeros).mp (riemann_hypothesis_is_the_line_hypothesis.mp h)
  · intro h
    exact riemann_hypothesis_is_the_line_hypothesis.mpr
      ((line_hypothesis_is_least_erasure Side (Nat → Frac) Side.flip Side.on side_flip_flip side_flip_fixed rfl
        zetaZeros).mpr h)

/-- AND THE RECORD OF THE ZEROS DECIDES NOTHING: for any height, no reading that respects the record returns the
    value on both the world of a zero registered on the line and the world of an off-line pair at that height. -/
theorem zeta_record_decides_nothing (γ : Nat → Frac) (g : (Side × (Nat → Frac) → Prop) → Prop)
    (hg : ∀ Z Z', SameRecord zetaSeat Z Z' → (g Z ↔ g Z')) :
    ¬ ((g (registered zetaSeat (Side.left, γ)) ↔ Value zetaSeat (registered zetaSeat (Side.left, γ))) ∧
       (g (pairWorld zetaSeat (Side.left, γ)) ↔ Value zetaSeat (pairWorld zetaSeat (Side.left, γ)))) := by
  have hoff : zetaSeat.σ (Side.left, γ) ≠ (Side.left, γ) := by
    intro e
    have e1 : Side.right = Side.left := congrArg Prod.fst e
    cases e1
  intro ⟨h1, h2⟩
  exact pair_world_lacks_value zetaSeat (Side.left, γ) hoff
    (h2.mp ((hg _ _ (one_record zetaSeat (Side.left, γ))).mp (h1.mpr (registered_has_value zetaSeat (Side.left, γ)))))

set_option maxRecDepth 100000 in
/-- THE DEFINITIONS COMPUTE WHAT THEY NAME, at small arguments: e to four terms is 65/24; the cosine and the sine of
    one are 13/24 and 5/6 at their first terms; the logarithm of two is 56/81 at two terms; and the first term of
    the series is one. -/
theorem definitions_compute :
    (expN 4 Frac.one).num * 24 = 65 * (((expN 4 Frac.one).den : Int) + 1) ∧
    (cosN 2 Frac.one).num * 24 = 13 * (((cosN 2 Frac.one).den : Int) + 1) ∧
    (sinN 1 Frac.one).num * 6 = 5 * (((sinN 1 Frac.one).den : Int) + 1) ∧
    (lnN 1 2).num * 81 = 56 * (((lnN 1 2).den : Int) + 1) ∧
    (etaRe 0 2 (fun _ => Frac.half) (fun _ => Frac.one)).num =
      (((etaRe 0 2 (fun _ => Frac.half) (fun _ => Frac.one)).den : Int) + 1) := by
  decide

/-! ## X · The eta identity at every finite stage: the algebra of the factor, on every commutative ring -/

/-- The alternating sum of the first 2N terms, taken in pairs: f 1 − f 2 + … + f (2N − 1) − f (2N). -/
def altPairs {R : Type} (add : R → R → R) (neg : R → R) (zero : R) (f : Nat → R) : Nat → R
  | 0 => zero
  | N + 1 => add (add (altPairs add neg zero f N) (f (2 * N + 1))) (neg (f (2 * N + 2)))

/-- The sum of the first 2N terms, taken in pairs. -/
def sumPairs {R : Type} (add : R → R → R) (zero : R) (f : Nat → R) : Nat → R
  | 0 => zero
  | N + 1 => add (add (sumPairs add zero f N) (f (2 * N + 1))) (f (2 * N + 2))

/-- The sum of the even terms f 2 + f 4 + … + f (2N). -/
def evenSum {R : Type} (add : R → R → R) (zero : R) (f : Nat → R) : Nat → R
  | 0 => zero
  | N + 1 => add (evenSum add zero f N) (f (2 * N + 2))

/-- The sum f 1 + … + f N. -/
def fullSum {R : Type} (add : R → R → R) (zero : R) (f : Nat → R) : Nat → R
  | 0 => zero
  | N + 1 => add (fullSum add zero f N) (f (N + 1))

theorem sum_swap_right {R : Type} (add : R → R → R)
    (hassoc : ∀ a b c, add (add a b) c = add a (add b c)) (hcomm : ∀ a b, add a b = add b a) (x y z : R) :
    add (add x y) z = add (add x z) y := by
  rw [hassoc x y z, hcomm y z, ← hassoc x z y]

theorem sum_interchange {R : Type} (add : R → R → R)
    (hassoc : ∀ a b c, add (add a b) c = add a (add b c)) (hcomm : ∀ a b, add a b = add b a) (x y z w : R) :
    add (add x y) (add z w) = add (add x z) (add y w) := by
  rw [hassoc x y (add z w), ← hassoc y z w, hcomm y z, hassoc z y w, ← hassoc x z (add y w)]

/-- One pair more: the step of the identity. -/
theorem eta_pair_step {R : Type} (add : R → R → R) (neg : R → R) (zero : R)
    (hassoc : ∀ a b c, add (add a b) c = add a (add b c)) (hcomm : ∀ a b, add a b = add b a)
    (hzero : ∀ a, add a zero = a) (hneg : ∀ a, add a (neg a) = zero)
    (A E P a b : R) (ih : add A (add E E) = P) :
    add (add (add A a) (neg b)) (add (add E b) (add E b)) = add (add P a) b := by
  rw [sum_interchange add hassoc hcomm E b E b,
      sum_interchange add hassoc hcomm (add A a) (neg b) (add E E) (add b b),
      sum_swap_right add hassoc hcomm A a (add E E), ih,
      ← hassoc (neg b) b b, hcomm (neg b) b, hneg b, hcomm zero b, hzero b]

/-- THE ALTERNATING SUM IS THE SUM LESS THE EVEN TERMS TWICE, at every stage, on every commutative ring, for every
    term: the alternating sum of the first 2N terms, with the even terms added twice, is the sum of the first 2N. -/
theorem alternating_pairs_identity {R : Type} (add : R → R → R) (neg : R → R) (zero : R)
    (hassoc : ∀ a b c, add (add a b) c = add a (add b c)) (hcomm : ∀ a b, add a b = add b a)
    (hzero : ∀ a, add a zero = a) (hneg : ∀ a, add a (neg a) = zero) (f : Nat → R) (N : Nat) :
    add (altPairs add neg zero f N) (add (evenSum add zero f N) (evenSum add zero f N)) = sumPairs add zero f N := by
  induction N with
  | zero =>
    show add zero (add zero zero) = zero
    rw [hzero zero, hzero zero]
  | succ N ih =>
    show add (add (add (altPairs add neg zero f N) (f (2 * N + 1))) (neg (f (2 * N + 2))))
        (add (add (evenSum add zero f N) (f (2 * N + 2))) (add (evenSum add zero f N) (f (2 * N + 2))))
      = add (add (sumPairs add zero f N) (f (2 * N + 1))) (f (2 * N + 2))
    exact eta_pair_step add neg zero hassoc hcomm hzero hneg _ _ _ _ _ ih

/-- THE EVEN TERMS FACTOR: where f (2n) = c · f n, the even terms to 2N are c times the terms to N. -/
theorem even_terms_factor {R : Type} (add mul : R → R → R) (zero c : R)
    (hdist : ∀ a b, mul c (add a b) = add (mul c a) (mul c b)) (hmz : mul c zero = zero)
    (f : Nat → R) (hmult : ∀ n, f (2 * n + 2) = mul c (f (n + 1))) (N : Nat) :
    evenSum add zero f N = mul c (fullSum add zero f N) := by
  induction N with
  | zero =>
    show zero = mul c zero
    rw [hmz]
  | succ N ih =>
    show add (evenSum add zero f N) (f (2 * N + 2)) = mul c (add (fullSum add zero f N) (f (N + 1)))
    rw [ih, hmult N, hdist]

/-- THE ETA IDENTITY AT EVERY FINITE STAGE, on every commutative ring: for a term with f (2n) = c · f n, the
    alternating sum of the first 2N terms, with c times the first N terms added twice, is the sum of the first 2N.
    At f n = n^(−s) and c = 2^(−s) this reads η_2N = ζ_2N − 2^(1−s) ζ_N, the whole algebra of
    η(s) = (1 − 2^(1−s)) ζ(s). The citation of that identity carries the two limits and the continuation to the
    strip; the algebra is proved here. -/
theorem eta_identity_at_every_stage {R : Type} (add mul : R → R → R) (neg : R → R) (zero c : R)
    (hassoc : ∀ a b c, add (add a b) c = add a (add b c)) (hcomm : ∀ a b, add a b = add b a)
    (hzero : ∀ a, add a zero = a) (hneg : ∀ a, add a (neg a) = zero)
    (hdist : ∀ a b, mul c (add a b) = add (mul c a) (mul c b)) (hmz : mul c zero = zero)
    (f : Nat → R) (hmult : ∀ n, f (2 * n + 2) = mul c (f (n + 1))) (N : Nat) :
    add (altPairs add neg zero f N) (add (mul c (fullSum add zero f N)) (mul c (fullSum add zero f N)))
      = sumPairs add zero f N := by
  rw [← even_terms_factor add mul zero c hdist hmz f hmult N]
  exact alternating_pairs_identity add neg zero hassoc hcomm hzero hneg f N

/-! ## XI · Where the kernel and its twin meet -/

/-- The series at one half plus two i: three terms, eight inner terms. -/
def meetRe : Frac := etaRe 2 8 (fun _ => Frac.half) (fun _ => ⟨2, 0⟩)
def meetIm : Frac := etaIm 2 8 (fun _ => Frac.half) (fun _ => ⟨2, 0⟩)

/-- THE SERIES OF THIS KERNEL, COMPUTED TO TWENTY PLACES AT ONE POINT: at one half plus two i, three terms, eight
    inner terms, the real part lies strictly between 0.53180207690295243439 and that plus 2·10^(−20), the imaginary part between
    0.22737850912720984721 and that plus 2·10^(−20). The twin computes the same finite sums in its own arithmetic and is held to
    these brackets: the place where the definitions above and the executed series are one object. -/
theorem series_meet_the_twin :
    (53180207690295243439 : Int) * ((meetRe.den : Int) + 1) < meetRe.num * 100000000000000000000 ∧
    meetRe.num * 100000000000000000000 < ((53180207690295243439 : Int) + 2) * ((meetRe.den : Int) + 1) ∧
    (22737850912720984721 : Int) * ((meetIm.den : Int) + 1) < meetIm.num * 100000000000000000000 ∧
    meetIm.num * 100000000000000000000 < ((22737850912720984721 : Int) + 2) * ((meetIm.den : Int) + 1) := by
  decide +kernel

end USeat
